# File: api/README.md

# API Reference

Everything Dialex exports, by entry point. Every entry point is a subpath of the `dialexjs` package (`import { DialexProvider } from "dialexjs/react"`); the programmatic API of the CLI is `@dialexjs/cli/api`. Nothing is exported from the package root other than what [Core](./core.md) lists, so a framework adapter is only loaded when you import it.

## Entry points

| Entry point                                                                              | What it provides                                                     | Reference                                                             |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dialexjs`                                                                               | Config, dictionaries, `createT`, formatting helpers, ICU and types   | [Core](./core.md), [Formatting](./formatting.md), [Types](./types.md) |
| `dialexjs/icu`                                                                           | The ICU message parser and formatter without the rest of the runtime | [ICU messages](./icu.md)                                              |
| `dialexjs/server`                                                                        | `getDictionary` and `getT` for server code                           | [Server adapters](./server-adapters.md#dialexjs-server)               |
| `dialexjs/express`, `fastify`, `koa`, `hono`, `elysia`, `h3`, `hapi`, `adonis`, `nestjs` | Request middleware, plugins and modules                              | [Server adapters](./server-adapters.md)                               |
| `dialexjs/sveltekit`, `astro`, `trpc`, `web`                                             | Hook, middleware, context and Fetch API handler                      | [Server adapters](./server-adapters.md)                               |
| `dialexjs/react`, `preact`, `solid`, `vue`, `nuxt`, `svelte`, `qwik`, `lit`, `angular`   | Providers, hooks and stores of the client frameworks                 | [Client frameworks](./client-frameworks.md)                           |
| `dialexjs/react-native`                                                                  | `DialexProvider` with device locales and storage                     | [Client frameworks](./client-frameworks.md#dialexjs-react-native)     |
| `dialexjs/next/middleware`, `dialexjs/next/link`                                         | Next.js middleware and `DialexLink`                                  | [Client frameworks](./client-frameworks.md#next-js)                   |
| `dialexjs/routing`                                                                       | Locale-prefixed paths, `hreflang` links and sitemap entries          | [Routing](./routing.md)                                               |
| `dialexjs/testing`, `dialexjs/testing/react`, `dialexjs/testing/vue`                     | Test contexts, mock requests and test providers                      | [Testing](./testing.md)                                               |
| `@dialexjs/cli/api`                                                                      | Project analysis and the dictionary editing helpers                  | [CLI API](./cli-api.md)                                               |

## Conventions

- **Typed names and paths.** `DictionaryRegistry`, `Register` and `MessageArguments` are empty interfaces that `dialex generate` augments in `dialex-env.d.ts`. Until it has run, dictionary names and `t()` paths are plain `string`; afterwards they autocomplete and are checked. See [Types](./types.md).
- **The generated `dialex` object.** Providers, adapters and `createDialexServer` accept `{ ...dialex }` from `dialex.generated.ts`. It carries the dictionaries, the client-safe config and, with lazy loading, the loaders, so locale settings are written once, in `dialex.config.ts`.
- **Failures.** A missing dictionary, locale or path never throws in production code: it logs `console.warn` with a `[dialex]` prefix and returns an empty object or the path itself. Invalid ICU messages are reported and returned unchanged by `t()`; `formatMessage` throws. Hooks that need a provider throw when it is missing.
- **Stability.** Dialex is below 1.0. Breaking changes ship in minor releases and are listed in the [changelog](../guide/changelog.md).

# File: api/cli-api.md

# CLI API

`@dialexjs/cli/api` is the programmatic API the [VS Code extension](../guide/vscode.md) and the language server are built on. It reads dictionaries and configs from the syntax tree and **does not run project code**, except for the two opt-in functions marked below.

```ts
import { analyzeProject, readStaticConfig } from "@dialexjs/cli/api";
```

## Analysis

### `analyzeProject(options)`

```ts
function analyzeProject(options: AnalysisOptions): Promise<AnalysisResult>;
```

Finds the dictionaries of a project, checks locale parity, ICU messages, lock-file staleness and references from source code, and returns the issues. `dialex check` is a thin layer over it.

| Option     | Type                  | Default               | Description                                                                                                                     |
| ---------- | --------------------- | --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `root`     | `string`              | —                     | The project folder. Required                                                                                                    |
| `config`   | `AnalysisConfig`      | —                     | `defaultLocale`, `locales`, `include`, `exclude`. Required                                                                      |
| `src`      | `string[]`            | `DEFAULT_SOURCE_GLOB` | Source globs to scan for references. Pass `[]` to skip scanning                                                                 |
| `runtime`  | `boolean`             | `false`               | **Runs project code.** Imports dictionaries the syntax tree cannot describe (spreads, computed keys). Editors must leave it off |
| `ignore`   | `string[]`            | —                     | More ignore globs, relative to `root` (nested projects)                                                                         |
| `unused`   | `boolean`             | `true`                | Report possibly unused keys and dictionaries                                                                                    |
| `lock`     | `boolean`             | `true`                | Report translations whose source text changed since `dialex.lock.json`                                                          |
| `cache`    | `AnalysisCache`       | —                     | Reuse parsed dictionaries and scanned sources between calls. Ignored with `runtime`                                             |
| `contents` | `Map<string, string>` | —                     | Unsaved text of files by absolute path, read instead of the file on disk. For linters and editors                               |

The result:

| Field                | Type                   | Description                                                                           |
| -------------------- | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `issues`             | `AnalysisIssue[]`      | Everything found. See the table below                                                 |
| `dictionaries`       | `AnalyzedDictionary[]` | One entry per readable dictionary                                                     |
| `files`              | `string[]`             | Absolute paths of every dictionary file that matched                                  |
| `sourceFilesScanned` | `number`               | How many source files were scanned for references                                     |
| `inlineDictionaries` | `string[]`             | Names registered in code with `dictionaries: { name: ... }`. Empty when `src` is `[]` |

An `AnalysisIssue` has `file`, `level` (`"error" \| "warning" \| "info"`), `code` ([see the codes](../guide/diagnostics.md)), `message`, and, when known, `range` (zero-based `{ start, end }` of `{ line, column }`), `dictionary`, `locale`, `path`, and `sourceLocale` (for `missing-key`: a locale to copy the key from).

An `AnalyzedDictionary` has `name`, `file`, `locales`, `leaves` (`locale -> dotted path -> { kind, value? }`), `paths` (the union of dotted paths) and, when read statically, `df` for editing.

### Other analysis exports

| Export                        | Description                                                                                                                                                        |
| ----------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `createAnalysisCache()`       | An `AnalysisCache` for a long-lived caller. It reuses what has not changed (keyed by modification time and size)                                                   |
| `analyzeProjectSync(options)` | `analyzeProject` for callers that cannot await, such as lint rules. Reads dictionaries from the syntax tree only: `runtime` is ignored, so project code never runs |
| `clearGitignore(cache)`       | Forgets the cached `.gitignore` rules, for example after a `.gitignore` changed                                                                                    |
| `scanReferences(text)`        | Finds `getDictionary("x")`-style and `t("x.y.z")` references in source text. Returns `{ kind, value, start, end }[]`                                               |
| `scanText(text)`              | Like `scanReferences`, and also returns the dictionary names the text registers inline. Returns `{ references, inline }`                                           |
| `relativeFile(root, file)`    | A root-relative path with forward slashes, for display                                                                                                             |
| `DEFAULT_SOURCE_GLOB`         | `**/*.{ts,tsx,js,jsx,mjs,cjs,vue,svelte,astro,mdx}`                                                                                                                |

## Scanning files

| Export                                | Description                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `scanFiles(root, patterns, options?)` | Finds files under `root`, skipping build output, configured excludes and Git-ignored paths. Options: `kind`, `exclude`, `ignore`, `gitignore`, `gitignoreFilter` |
| `createGitignoreFilter(root)`         | A function that says whether an absolute path is ignored by Git, reading `.gitignore` files of the project, its parents and nested folders                       |
| `BUILTIN_IGNORE`                      | Folders that never hold dictionaries or sources                                                                                                                  |
| `SOURCE_BUILTIN_IGNORE`               | What the source scan skips on top: other tools' output, declarations, generated and config files                                                                 |

## Editing dictionaries

The helpers work on the syntax tree and keep the rest of the file, comments and formatting included.

| Export                                                     | Description                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `parseDictionaryText(file, text)`                          | Parses dictionary source text (an unsaved buffer, for example). `undefined` when the shape is not editable; throws on a syntax error |
| `loadDictionaryFile(file)`                                 | Loads a file. `undefined` when its shape is not editable                                                                             |
| `renderDictionaryFile(df)`                                 | The source text with all edits applied, without writing                                                                              |
| `saveDictionaryFile(df)`                                   | Writes the edited file                                                                                                               |
| `listLocales(df)`, `listLeaves(df, locale)`                | The locales, and every leaf `{ path, kind, value? }` of a locale in source order                                                     |
| `hasPath(df, locale, path)`, `getString(df, locale, path)` | Whether a key exists, and its string value                                                                                           |
| `setString(df, locale, path, value)`                       | Sets or creates a string. Returns `"created"`, `"updated"` or `"skipped"` (functions are never overwritten)                          |
| `copyLeaf(df, from, to, path, mapString?)`                 | Copies a leaf between locales, optionally rewriting strings. `false` when there is nothing to copy or the target has the key         |
| `locationOf(df, locale, path?)`                            | The range of a locale's or a key's property name                                                                                     |
| `dictionaryLocation(df)`                                   | The range of the object whose keys are locales                                                                                       |
| `getLeafSource(df, locale, path)`                          | The source code of a leaf's value                                                                                                    |
| `TODO_PREFIX`                                              | `"[TODO] "`: what `--fix` puts before copied strings                                                                                 |

## Configuration

| Export                           | Description                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `readStaticConfig(root, file?)`  | Reads `dialex.config.*` from its syntax tree: `{ config, file?, notes }`. `notes` lists settings that are not literals and were left at their defaults |
| `parseStaticConfig(text, file?)` | The same for source text                                                                                                                               |
| `DEFAULT_STATIC_CONFIG`          | The defaults used when a setting cannot be read                                                                                                        |

## Projects and generation

| Export                                                          | Description                                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `loadStaticProject(root, configFile?)`                          | The config (from the syntax tree) and every dictionary file, ready for reading and editing. Runs no project code |
| `loadProject(root, configFile?)`                                | **Runs project code**: evaluates `dialex.config.*` before loading the dictionaries                               |
| `toKey(dictionary, path)`                                       | `("home", ["nav", "about"])` becomes `"home.nav.about"`                                                          |
| `renderGenerated(root, options?)`                               | Works out `dialex.generated.ts` and `dialex-env.d.ts` without writing, to see whether they are current           |
| `generateDictionaries(root, options?)`                          | Writes the generated files. `options.static` reads the config without running it                                 |
| `startGenerateWatcher(root, options, regenerate, delay?, log?)` | Regenerates when a dictionary or config file is added, edited or removed                                         |

## Lock file

| Export                                    | Description                                                                                    |
| ----------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `LOCK_FILE`                               | `"dialex.lock.json"`                                                                           |
| `readLock(root)`, `writeLock(root, lock)` | Reads the lock (or `undefined`) and writes it with sorted keys                                 |
| `hashSource(text)`                        | The short fingerprint stored for a source string                                               |
| `isStale(lock, locale, key, text)`        | `true` when the key was recorded from different source text. A key with no record is not stale |

## Types

`AnalysisCache`, `AnalysisConfig`, `AnalysisIssue`, `AnalysisOptions`, `AnalysisResult`, `AnalyzedDictionary`, `IssueCode`, `IssueLevel`, `LeafInfo`, `Reference`, `ScanOptions`, `Lockfile`, `DictionaryFile`, `Leaf`, `LeafKind`, `SourceRange`, `StaticConfig`, `StaticConfigResult`, `Project`, `ProjectDictionary`, `GenerateOptions`, `RenderedGenerate`.

# File: api/client-frameworks.md

# Client frameworks

The adapters for UI frameworks: a provider (or plugin) that holds the active locale, and hooks or stores that read dictionaries and `t`. Guides with complete examples are on the [framework pages](../frameworks/README.md).

## Shared options

Most providers take the generated `dialex` object (`dictionaries`, `config`, `loaders`: `{ ...dialex }`) and these options:

| Option           | Type                                  | Default                 | Description                                                                                                            |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `defaultLocale`  | `string`                              | the config, then `"en"` | Locale used when nothing else decides                                                                                  |
| `initialLocale`  | `string`                              | —                       | The locale to render first, for example the one the server resolved. When set, the remembered locale is not applied    |
| `persist`        | `"cookie" \| "localStorage" \| false` | `"cookie"`              | Where the choice is remembered. It is applied after mount, so server-rendered markup and the first client render agree |
| `storageKey`     | `string`                              | `"locale"`              | Cookie or `localStorage` key                                                                                           |
| `onLocaleChange` | `(locale: string) => void`            | —                       | Called after the locale changes                                                                                        |

Hooks and stores return the dictionary for the active locale following the [fallback chain](../guide/fallbacks.md). With `lazy` loading, name the dictionaries a `t` will read (`useT("home", "nav")`) so they are loaded; the component updates when they arrive.

## React

`dialexjs/react`

| Export                | Signature                                      | Description                                                                                              |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DialexProvider`      | `(props: DialexProviderProps) => ReactElement` | Provides locale, `setLocale` and dictionaries. Props: the shared options, `children` and `{ ...dialex }` |
| `useDialex`           | `() => { locale, setLocale, store }`           | The context. Throws outside a provider                                                                   |
| `useDialexConfig`     | `() => DialexClientConfig`                     | The generated config, for `locales` or `prefixDefault`                                                   |
| `useDictionary`       | `<K>(name: K) => ResolveDictionaryType<K>`     | The dictionary for the active locale. With `lazy` it suspends until loaded: use `<Suspense>`             |
| `useT`                | `(...dictionaryNames: string[]) => Translate`  | A `t` bound to the active locale                                                                         |
| `preloadDictionaries` | see [below](#preloaddictionaries)              | Starts loading lazy dictionaries                                                                         |

## Preact

`dialexjs/preact` has the same exports as React (`DialexProvider`, `useDialex`, `useDialexConfig`, `useDictionary`, `useT`, `preloadDictionaries`) with `ComponentChildren` props. With `lazy` the dictionary is an empty object until it has loaded, and the component re-renders when it arrives; it does not suspend. It works without `preact/compat`.

## Solid

`dialexjs/solid`

| Export                | Description                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DialexProvider`      | Props: the shared options, `children` and `{ ...dialex }`                                                                         |
| `useDialex()`         | `{ locale, setLocale, store, loaded, ensureLoaded }`. `locale` is an accessor: read it as `locale()`                              |
| `useDictionary(name)` | An accessor: `const home = useDictionary("home")`, then `home().title`. Updates on locale change and when a lazy dictionary loads |
| `useT(...names)`      | A `t` that follows the current locale. Call it in JSX or an effect so the result is reactive                                      |
| `preloadDictionaries` | See [below](#preloaddictionaries)                                                                                                 |

## Vue

`dialexjs/vue`

| Export                | Signature                                                   | Description                                                                                  |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createDialex`        | `(options?: CreateDialexOptions) => Plugin & DialexContext` | The plugin. Options: `{ ...dialex }`, `defaultLocale`, `onLocaleChange`                      |
| `useDialex`           | `() => { locale: Ref<string>, setLocale, store }`           | The context. Throws when the plugin is not installed                                         |
| `useDictionary`       | `<K>(name: K) => ComputedRef<ResolveDictionaryType<K>>`     | The dictionary as a computed ref. With `lazy` it is empty until loaded, and SSR waits for it |
| `useT`                | `(...dictionaryNames: string[]) => Translate`               | A `t` that follows the locale. Read it in a template or `computed`                           |
| `DIALEX_KEY`          | `InjectionKey<DialexContext>`                               | The injection key of the context                                                             |
| `preloadDictionaries` | See [below](#preloaddictionaries)                           | Starts loading lazy dictionaries                                                             |

## Nuxt

`dialexjs/nuxt` is a Nuxt module: `modules: ["dialexjs/nuxt"]`. It installs the Vue plugin with a cookie-backed locale from `dialex.generated.ts` and auto-imports `useDialex` and `useDictionary`. Options go under the `dialex` key of `nuxt.config.ts`:

| Option       | Type     | Default    | Description                                                                                                  |
| ------------ | -------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `cookieName` | `string` | `"locale"` | Cookie that remembers the locale                                                                             |
| `generated`  | `string` | found      | Path of the generated file, without the extension. Found in the source directory, the project root or `src/` |

It also accepts the `DialexConfig` fields. Run `dialex generate` first: the module reads the file it writes.

## Svelte

`dialexjs/svelte`

| Export                                  | Description                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `provideDialex(source?, options?)`      | Call once in the root component with `{ ...dialex }`. Returns `DialexSvelte`          |
| `useDialex()`                           | `{ locale, setLocale, store, dictionary, translator }` of the nearest `provideDialex` |
| `useDictionary(name)`                   | A store: `const home = useDictionary("home")`, then `$home.title`                     |
| `useT(...names)`                        | A store of `t`: `const t = useT("home")`, then `$t("home.title")`                     |
| `createSvelteDialex(source?, options?)` | The reactive core without component context, for plain modules and tests              |
| `preloadDictionaries`                   | See [below](#preloaddictionaries)                                                     |

`options` are the shared options (`defaultLocale`, `initialLocale`, `persist`, `storageKey`, `onLocaleChange`).

## Qwik

`dialexjs/qwik`

```ts
function createDialexQwik(options?: CreateDialexQwikOptions): {
  useDialexProvider(options?: UseDialexProviderOptions): DialexState;
  useDialex(): DialexState;
  setLocale(state: DialexState, locale: string): void;
  useDictionary<K>(name: K): () => ResolveDictionaryType<K>;
  useT(): Translate;
  getPersistedLocale(): string | undefined;
};
```

Call `createDialexQwik({ ...dialex })` once in a module of its own and import the hooks from there; the dictionaries then stay out of the serialized page. `DialexState` is `{ locale: string; loaded: number }`, plain data Qwik can resume. `persist` and `storageKey` are the shared options; reading the stored locale back is up to the server (`getPersistedLocale`).

## Lit

`dialexjs/lit`

| Export                   | Description                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createDialex(options?)` | Creates the locale state: `{ locale, config, store, setLocale, subscribe, getDictionary, t }`. Create it once, in a module of its own                    |
| `DialexController`       | A reactive controller for any `ReactiveControllerHost`: `new DialexController(this, i18n)`. Has `locale`, `setLocale`, `dictionary(name)`, `t(...names)` |
| `preloadDictionaries`    | See [below](#preloaddictionaries)                                                                                                                        |

## `dialexjs/react-native`

| Export                                                                         | Description                                                                                  |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DialexProvider`                                                               | Provider for React Native and Expo. See the props below                                      |
| `useDialex`, `useDialexConfig`, `useDictionary`, `useT`, `preloadDictionaries` | The hooks of `dialexjs/react`                                                                |
| `LocaleStorage`                                                                | `{ getItem(key), setItem(key, value) }`, sync or async: AsyncStorage, MMKV or `localStorage` |

| Prop                                               | Type                 | Description                                                                                                          |
| -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `deviceLocales`                                    | `string \| string[]` | The device's languages, most preferred first (`expo-localization`'s `getLocales()`). The first supported one is used |
| `initialLocale`                                    | `string`             | Wins over `deviceLocales` and the stored locale                                                                      |
| `storage`                                          | `LocaleStorage`      | Where the choice is remembered. Children render once it has been read                                                |
| `storageKey`                                       | `string`             | Storage key. Default `"locale"`                                                                                      |
| `defaultLocale`, `onLocaleChange`, `{ ...dialex }` | —                    | As in the shared options                                                                                             |

## Angular

`dialexjs/angular`

| Export                     | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `provideDialex(options)`   | Environment providers. `AngularDialexOptions`: `dictionaries` (required), `config`, `defaultLocale`, `locales`, `fallbacks`, `initialLocale` (a string, or a function that runs in the injection context), `persist`, `storageKey` |
| `injectDialex()`           | The `DialexStore`: `locale` (a signal), `setLocale`, `dictionary(name)`, `t`                                                                                                                                                       |
| `injectDictionary(name)`   | The dictionary as a signal                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `injectT()`                | The `t` function; it reads the locale signal on every call, so a template using it stays current                                                                                                                                   |
| `DIALEX`, `DIALEX_OPTIONS` | The injection tokens of the store and of the options                                                                                                                                                                               |

Call the `inject*` functions in an injection context.

## Next.js

| Export                                                         | Description                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `createDialexMiddleware(options)` (`dialexjs/next/middleware`) | Keeps every page under a locale prefix. Returns `(request: NextRequest) => NextResponse`                            |
| `DialexLink` (`dialexjs/next/link`)                            | `next/link` that keeps the locale in the URL. Needs `DialexProvider` above it. Props: `next/link`'s, plus `locale?` |

`createDialexMiddleware` options: the [routing options](./routing.md) (`locales` required, `defaultLocale`, `prefixDefault`), the detection options `queryKeys`, `cookieKeys`, `headerKey`, `custom`, `fallbacks`, and:

| Option       | Type                            | Default                           | Description                                                        |
| ------------ | ------------------------------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `cookieName` | `string`                        | `"locale"`                        | Cookie that remembers the visitor's locale                         |
| `setCookie`  | `boolean`                       | `true`                            | Write the cookie when the URL's locale differs from the stored one |
| `ignore`     | `(pathname: string) => boolean` | `/_next`, `/api`, file extensions | Paths that skip locale handling                                    |

## Types

The option and prop types, and which entry point uses them:

| Type                                                                 | Used by                                                                    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DialexProviderProps`                                                | `DialexProvider` of `dialexjs/react`, `preact`, `solid` and `react-native` |
| `DialexContext`                                                      | `useDialex()` of `dialexjs/react`, `preact`, `solid` and `vue`             |
| `CreateDialexOptions`                                                | `createDialex` of `dialexjs/vue` and `dialexjs/lit`                        |
| `Dialex`                                                             | The state `createDialex` of `dialexjs/lit` returns                         |
| `DialexOptions`, `DialexSvelte`                                      | `provideDialex` and `createSvelteDialex` of `dialexjs/svelte`              |
| `CreateDialexQwikOptions`, `UseDialexProviderOptions`, `DialexState` | `createDialexQwik` and its hooks, `dialexjs/qwik`                          |
| `AngularDialexOptions`, `DialexStore`                                | `provideDialex` and `injectDialex` of `dialexjs/angular`                   |
| `NuxtDialexOptions`                                                  | The module options of `dialexjs/nuxt`                                      |
| `DialexLinkProps`, `DialexMiddlewareOptions`                         | `DialexLink` and `createDialexMiddleware` of Next.js                       |
| `LocaleStorage`                                                      | The `storage` prop of `dialexjs/react-native`                              |

## `preloadDictionaries`

```ts
function preloadDictionaries(
  source: DialexSource,
  ...rest: (string | { locale?: string })[]
): Promise<void>;
```

Starts loading lazy dictionaries; it does nothing when they are not lazy. In `lazy: "locale"` mode it loads the default locale unless you pass `{ locale }` first.

```ts
await preloadDictionaries(dialex, { locale: "tr" }, "checkout", "cart");
```

# File: api/core.md

# Core

The `dialexjs` entry point: configuration, dictionaries and the `t` function. The formatting helpers are on [Formatting](./formatting.md), the types on [Types](./types.md).

## `defineConfig(config)`

```ts
function defineConfig(config: DialexConfig): DialexConfig;
```

Gives `dialex.config.ts` its types and returns the object unchanged.

```ts
// dialex.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "dialexjs";

export default defineConfig({ defaultLocale: "en", locales: ["en", "tr"] });
```

See [Configuration](../guide/configuration.md) for every option.

## `defineDictionary(name, dictionary)`

```ts
function defineDictionary<N extends string, D extends Record<string, any>>(
  name: N,
  dictionary: D,
): DictionaryDefinition<N, D[keyof D]>;

function defineDictionary<N extends string, D extends Record<string, any>>(config: {
  name: N;
  dictionary: D;
}): DictionaryDefinition<N, D[keyof D]>;
```

| Parameter    | Description                                                                                                                     |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `name`       | The dictionary name: the first segment of every `t()` path and the argument of `getDictionary`. It must be unique and a literal |
| `dictionary` | An object that maps each locale to its content: strings, nested objects, or functions                                           |

It registers the dictionary in [`globalDictionaries`](#globaldictionaries) and returns `{ name, dictionary }`. Put each dictionary in its own `*.content.ts` file as the default export, so `dialex generate` finds it. See [Dictionaries](../guide/dictionaries.md).

```ts
// src/home.content.ts
import { defineDictionary } from "dialexjs";

export default defineDictionary("home", {
  en: { title: "Welcome", greeting: (name: string) => `Hello, ${name}!` },
  tr: { title: "Hoş geldiniz", greeting: (name: string) => `Merhaba, ${name}!` },
});
```

<a id="createt"></a>

## `createT(getDictionary, locale?)`

```ts
function createT(getDictionary: (name: any) => any, locale?: string): Translate;
```

Builds a `t("dictionary.key.path", ...args)` function on top of a `getDictionary(name)` accessor. The framework adapters do this for you; call it yourself in a script or a test.

| Parameter       | Description                                                        |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `getDictionary` | Returns the content of the dictionary called `name` for the locale |
| `locale`        | The locale used to format ICU messages. Default `"en"`             |

What `t(path, ...args)` returns:

| The path leads to                         | Result                                                                         |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| A function                                | `fn(...args)`: the extra arguments go to the function                          |
| A string and no values object             | The string as it is. Nothing is parsed                                         |
| A string and a values object (`{ n: 3 }`) | The string formatted as an [ICU message](../guide/icu.md) for `locale`         |
| Nothing                                   | `console.warn("[dialex] Translation path ... not found.")` and the path itself |

A string that cannot be formatted (invalid ICU, or a missing value) is reported with `console.warn` and returned unchanged, so one bad string never crashes a page. See [Key Paths](../guide/key-paths.md).

## `globalDictionaries`

```ts
const globalDictionaries: Record<string, Record<string, any>>;
```

The in-process registry that `defineDictionary` fills. Adapters read it when you do not pass `dictionaries` to them. It is empty until the dictionary files have been imported, which is why the generated `dialex` object is the reliable way to pass dictionaries.

## `DEFAULT_CONFIG`

```ts
const DEFAULT_CONFIG: {
  defaultLocale: string; // "en"
  locales: string[]; // []
  include: string | string[]; // "**/*.content.ts"
  fallbacks: Record<string, string[]>; // {}
  prefixDefault: boolean; // true
  lazy: boolean | "locale"; // false
};
```

What every tool uses for a setting, or the whole config file, that is missing. `locales` is empty: `dialex generate` then uses the locales your dictionaries define.

## Configuration types

### `DialexConfig`

The shape of `dialex.config.ts`. Every field is optional.

| Field           | Type                       | Default             | Description                                                                           |
| --------------- | -------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `defaultLocale` | `string`                   | `"en"`              | Locale used when none can be resolved                                                 |
| `locales`       | `string[]`                 | —                   | Supported locales                                                                     |
| `include`       | `string \| string[]`       | `"**/*.content.ts"` | Glob(s) of the dictionary files                                                       |
| `exclude`       | `string[]`                 | —                   | Globs that are never scanned, on top of `node_modules`, build output and `.gitignore` |
| `output`        | `string`                   | `src/` or the root  | Where `dialex.generated.ts` is written                                                |
| `configFile`    | `string`                   | —                   | Custom path of the config file                                                        |
| `fallbacks`     | `Record<string, string[]>` | —                   | Explicit [fallback chains](../guide/fallbacks.md)                                     |
| `prefixDefault` | `boolean`                  | `true`              | Whether the default locale also gets a URL prefix                                     |
| `lazy`          | `boolean \| "locale"`      | `false`             | Load dictionaries on demand. See [Lazy Loading](../guide/lazy-loading.md)             |
| `lint`          | `LintConfig`               | —                   | Level and options of each check. See [Linting](../guide/linting.md)                   |
| `translate`     | `TranslateConfig`          | —                   | Settings of [`dialex translate`](../cli/translate.md)                                 |

### `LintConfig`

| Field   | Type                              | Description                                                                    |
| ------- | --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `rules` | `Record<string, LintRuleSetting>` | Level and options per diagnostic code, plus `dynamic-key` and `literal-string` |

A `LintRuleSetting` is a `LintSeverity` (`"off"`, `"warn"` or `"error"`), or `[LintSeverity, options]` for checks that take options. `dialex check`, the editors and [`@dialexjs/eslint-plugin`](../guide/linting.md) all read it.

### `TranslateConfig`

| Field          | Type                | Description                                               |
| -------------- | ------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
| `provider`     | `TranslateProvider` | The backend that translates strings. Required             |
| `sourceLocale` | `string`            | The locale to translate from. Defaults to `defaultLocale` |

### `TranslateProvider`

```ts
interface TranslateProvider {
  name?: string;
  supportsIcu?: boolean;
  translate(texts: string[], from: string, to: string): Promise<string[]>;
}
```

`translate` receives plain strings and must return one translation per input, in the same order. Set `supportsIcu` only when the provider keeps the structure of `plural` and `select` messages intact; messages with that syntax are not sent to providers that do not. See [`dialex translate`](../cli/translate.md).

## Generated file types

| Type                 | Description                                                                                                                                                       |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DialexSource`       | What the generated `dialex` export holds and providers accept: `dictionaries`, `config` and, in lazy mode, `loaders`                                              |
| `DialexClientConfig` | The settings `dialex generate` copies into `dialex.generated.ts`: `defaultLocale`, `locales`, `fallbacks`, `prefixDefault`, `lazy`. `translate` is never included |
| `DictionaryLoader`   | `() => Promise<any>`: loads one dictionary, or one locale of it                                                                                                   |
| `DictionaryLoaders`  | Loaders by dictionary name. With `lazy: "locale"` a dictionary maps each locale to its own loader                                                                 |


---

# File: api/formatting.md

# Formatting

Locale-aware helpers built on `Intl`, exported from `dialexjs`. Every `Intl` formatter is created once per locale and options and reused, so calling a helper in a render function or a request handler is cheap. For messages with arguments use [ICU messages](./icu.md); these helpers are for values you format yourself, typically inside a function message.

## `plural(locale, count, forms)`

```ts
function plural<T = string>(locale: string, count: number, forms: PluralForms<T>): T;
```

Picks the form for `count` with the locale's CLDR rules. `forms.other` is required and is used when the locale's category has no form of its own.

```ts
items: (n: number) => plural("en", n, { one: "1 item", other: `${n} items` });
```

## `number(locale, value, options?)`

```ts
function number(locale: string, value: number, options?: Intl.NumberFormatOptions): string;
```

```ts
number("de", 1234.5); // "1.234,5"
number("en", 0.25, { style: "percent" }); // "25%"
number("tr", 9.9, { style: "currency", currency: "TRY" }); // "₺9,90"
```

## `date(locale, value, options?)`

```ts
function date(
  locale: string,
  value: Date | number | string,
  options?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions,
): string;
```

`value` may be a `Date`, a timestamp or anything `new Date(value)` accepts.

```ts
date("en", new Date(2026, 2, 1), { dateStyle: "medium" }); // "Mar 1, 2026"
```

## `relativeTime(locale, value, unit, options?)`

```ts
function relativeTime(
  locale: string,
  value: number,
  unit: Intl.RelativeTimeFormatUnit,
  options?: Intl.RelativeTimeFormatOptions,
): string;
```

A negative `value` is in the past.

```ts
relativeTime("en", -2, "day"); // "2 days ago"
relativeTime("en", 1, "day", { numeric: "auto" }); // "tomorrow"
```

## `list(locale, values, options?)`

```ts
function list(locale: string, values: Iterable<string>, options?: Intl.ListFormatOptions): string;
```

```ts
list("en", ["a", "b", "c"]); // "a, b, and c"
list("de", ["a", "b", "c"]); // "a, b und c"
```

## `formatters(locale)`

```ts
function formatters(locale: string): Formatters;
```

The five helpers above with the locale already bound.

```ts
const f = formatters("tr");
f.number(1234.5); // "1.234,5"
```

## Types

| Type             | Definition                                                                                  |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PluralCategory` | `"zero" \| "one" \| "two" \| "few" \| "many" \| "other"`                                    |
| `PluralForms<T>` | `{ other: T } & Partial<Record<"zero" \| "one" \| "two" \| "few" \| "many", T>>`            |
| `Formatters`     | `{ plural, number, date, relativeTime, list }` with the `locale` argument removed from each |

See [Formatting & Plurals](../guide/formatting.md) for when to use these and when an ICU message is the better choice.


---

# File: api/icu.md

# ICU messages

The ICU MessageFormat parser and formatter. `dialexjs` re-exports `formatMessage`, `parseMessage`, the error classes and the node and value types; `dialexjs/icu` additionally exports the introspection helpers and does not load the rest of the runtime. For the message syntax itself see [ICU Messages](../guide/icu.md).

```ts
import { formatMessage } from "dialexjs/icu";
```

## `formatMessage(locale, message, values?)`

```ts
function formatMessage(locale: string, message: string | IcuNode[], values?: IcuValues): string;
```

| Parameter | Description                                             |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locale`  | The BCP 47 tag used for plural rules, numbers and dates |
| `message` | The message text, or nodes returned by `parseMessage`   |
| `values`  | The arguments by name. Default `{}`                     |

```ts
formatMessage("en", "{count, plural, =0 {No items} one {# item} other {# items}}", { count: 3 });
// "3 items"
```

A string message is compiled once and cached (up to 500 distinct messages), so formatting the same message again does no parsing.

| Throws           | When                                                                                             |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `IcuSyntaxError` | The message is not valid ICU                                                                     |
| `IcuFormatError` | A value is missing, or a `plural`/`number` argument is not a finite number, or a date is invalid |

## `parseMessage(message)`

```ts
function parseMessage(message: string): IcuNode[];
```

Parses a message into nodes and throws `IcuSyntaxError` with the position of the problem. Use it to validate a message or to inspect its arguments.

## `getArguments(nodes)`

```ts
function getArguments(nodes: IcuNode[]): IcuArgument[];
```

Lists the distinct arguments of a parsed message, including those in nested branches, in order of first appearance.

```ts
getArguments(parseMessage("{n, plural, one {# file} other {# files}} for {name}"));
// [{ name: "n", type: "plural", selectors: ["one", "other"] }, { name: "name", type: "argument" }]
```

## `argumentSignature(nodes)`

```ts
function argumentSignature(nodes: IcuNode[]): string;
```

A comparable description of a message's arguments that ignores the text of plural and select branches. Two translations of one key have the same signature when they use the same arguments; `dialex check` uses it to report `icu-args-mismatch`.

## `isIcuStructured(message)`

```ts
function isIcuStructured(message: string): boolean;
```

Whether a message uses `plural`, `selectordinal`, `select`, `number`, `date` or `time`, as opposed to plain `{name}` placeholders. It decides how strictly a parse error is treated.

## `findPlurals(nodes)`

```ts
function findPlurals(nodes: IcuNode[]): Extract<IcuNode, { type: "plural" }>[];
```

Every `plural` and `selectordinal` node of a parsed message, including nested ones. `dialex check` uses it to find plural categories a language needs but the message lacks.

## Types and errors

| Name              | Description                                                                                                      |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `IcuNode`         | A node of a parsed message: `literal`, `argument`, `number`, `date`, `time`, `plural`, `select` or `pound` (`#`) |
| `IcuValue`        | `string \| number \| boolean \| Date \| null \| undefined`                                                       |
| `IcuValues`       | `Record<string, IcuValue>`                                                                                       |
| `IcuArgument`     | `{ name, type, selectors? }`: one argument of a message                                                          |
| `IcuArgumentType` | `"argument" \| "number" \| "date" \| "time" \| "plural" \| "selectordinal" \| "select"`                          |
| `IcuSyntaxError`  | Extends `Error`. `position` is the zero-based offset of the problem in the message                               |
| `IcuFormatError`  | Extends `Error`. Thrown for missing or invalid values                                                            |


---

# File: api/routing.md

# Routing

Pure helpers for locale-prefixed URLs, `hreflang` links and sitemaps. They have no framework dependency and run on the server and the client. For how to wire them into an app see [Routing Helpers](../guide/routing.md).

```ts
import { localizePath, stripLocale } from "dialexjs/routing";
```

## `RoutingOptions`

| Option          | Type       | Default | Description                                                                                            |
| --------------- | ---------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `locales`       | `string[]` | —       | Supported locales. Required                                                                            |
| `defaultLocale` | `string`   | —       | Locale used when a path has no prefix. Some helpers need it                                            |
| `prefixDefault` | `boolean`  | `true`  | Whether the default locale also gets a prefix. When `false` it lives at the unprefixed path (`/about`) |

## `localizePath(path, locale, options)`

```ts
function localizePath(path: string, locale: string, options: RoutingOptions): string;
```

Prefixes a path with a locale and replaces a locale prefix it already has. Query strings and fragments are kept. External URLs, `mailto:` links and bare `#fragments` are returned unchanged.

```ts
localizePath("/about", "tr", { locales: ["en", "tr"] }); // "/tr/about"
localizePath("/tr/about", "en", {
  locales: ["en", "tr"],
  defaultLocale: "en",
  prefixDefault: false,
}); // "/about"
```

## `stripLocale(path, locales)`

```ts
function stripLocale(path: string, locales: string[]): { path: string; locale?: string };
```

Removes a leading locale segment. Only an exact, case-insensitive match of `locales` counts, so `/english` is left alone.

```ts
stripLocale("/tr/about?x=1", ["en", "tr"]); // { path: "/about?x=1", locale: "tr" }
```

## `localeFromPath(path, options)`

```ts
function localeFromPath(path: string, options: RoutingOptions & { defaultLocale: string }): string;
```

The locale a path is under, or `defaultLocale` when it has no prefix.

```ts
localeFromPath("/tr/about", { locales: ["en", "tr"], defaultLocale: "en" }); // "tr"
localeFromPath("/about", { locales: ["en", "tr"], defaultLocale: "en" }); // "en"
```

## `isLocale(value, locales)`

```ts
function isLocale(value: string, locales: string[]): boolean;
```

Whether `value` is exactly one of `locales`.

## `alternateLinks(path, options)`

```ts
function alternateLinks(path: string, options: AlternateLinksOptions): AlternateLink[];
```

Builds one `hreflang` alternate per locale and, unless `xDefault` is `false`, an `x-default` entry for the default locale.

| Option     | Type      | Default | Description                                          |
| ---------- | --------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `baseUrl`  | `string`  | —       | Origin used for absolute URLs, `https://example.com` |
| `xDefault` | `boolean` | `true`  | Add an `x-default` entry                             |

It also takes every `RoutingOptions` field.

```ts
alternateLinks("/about", { locales: ["en", "tr"], baseUrl: "https://example.com" });
// [
//   { locale: "en", href: "https://example.com/en/about" },
//   { locale: "tr", href: "https://example.com/tr/about" },
//   { locale: "x-default", href: "https://example.com/en/about" },
// ]
```

## `alternateLanguages(path, options)`

```ts
function alternateLanguages(path: string, options: AlternateLinksOptions): Record<string, string>;
```

`alternateLinks` as a `{ [locale]: url }` map, the shape of Next.js `metadata.alternates.languages`.

## `sitemapEntries(paths, options)`

```ts
function sitemapEntries(
  paths: string[],
  options: AlternateLinksOptions & { lastModified?: string | Date },
): SitemapEntry[];
```

One entry per path and locale, each with its `hreflang` alternates, in the shape of Next.js `MetadataRoute.Sitemap`.

```ts
// app/sitemap.ts
export default function sitemap() {
  return sitemapEntries(["/", "/about"], {
    locales: ["en", "tr"],
    baseUrl: "https://example.com",
  });
}
```

## Types

| Type                    | Definition                                                                                          |
| ----------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AlternateLink`         | `{ locale: string; href: string }`. `locale` is `"x-default"` for the default entry                 |
| `AlternateLinksOptions` | `RoutingOptions` plus `baseUrl` and `xDefault`                                                      |
| `SitemapEntry`          | `{ url: string; lastModified?: string \| Date; alternates: { languages: Record<string, string> } }` |


---

# File: api/server-adapters.md

# Server adapters

Every server adapter resolves the request's locale, then adds `locale` and `getDictionary(name)` (and, where the framework allows, `t`) to the request. They share one set of options and one detection order. Guides with complete examples are on the [framework pages](../frameworks/README.md); how a locale is chosen is on [Locale Detection](../guide/locale-detection.md).

All adapters accept the generated object: `dialexExpress({ ...dialex })`.

## Options

Every adapter takes the locale detection options and, except `createDialexMiddleware` of Next.js and the NestJS module, the base adapter options.

### Locale detection options (`LocaleResolverOptions`)

| Option          | Type                                   | Default              | Description                                                                                                   |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `config`        | `GeneratedConfig`                      | —                    | The generated `config`. `{ ...dialex }` sets it. `defaultLocale`, `locales` and `fallbacks` below override it |
| `defaultLocale` | `string`                               | `"en"`               | Locale used when nothing matches                                                                              |
| `locales`       | `string[]`                             | —                    | Supported locales. Without it a path prefix is ignored and any candidate is accepted                          |
| `queryKeys`     | `string \| string[]`                   | `["locale", "lang"]` | Query parameter names                                                                                         |
| `cookieKeys`    | `string \| string[]`                   | `["locale", "lang"]` | Cookie names                                                                                                  |
| `headerKey`     | `string`                               | `"Accept-Language"`  | Header to read                                                                                                |
| `usePath`       | `boolean`                              | `true`               | Check the first URL path segment (`/tr/...`)                                                                  |
| `custom`        | `(req) => string \| null \| undefined` | —                    | Custom extractor, tried first. `req` is the framework's request object                                        |
| `fallbacks`     | `Record<string, string[]>`             | —                    | Explicit [fallback chains](../guide/fallbacks.md)                                                             |

### Base adapter options (`BaseAdapterOptions`)

| Option         | Type              | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| -------------- | ----------------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dictionaries` | `DictionaryInput` | —       | The generated `dictionaries`; `{ ...dialex }` sets it. Pass your own `{ name: { locale: content } }` map or array of `defineDictionary` results only when you do not use the generated file. Without either, only dictionaries already registered through `defineDictionary` are found |
| `setHeader`    | `boolean`         | `true`  | Send the resolved locale as `Content-Language`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |

## What each adapter adds

| Adapter                 | Import               | Registered with                                      | The request gets                                        |
| ----------------------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Express](#express)     | `dialexjs/express`   | `app.use(dialexExpress(options))`                    | `req.locale`, `req.getDictionary`, same on `res.locals` |
| [Fastify](#fastify)     | `dialexjs/fastify`   | `app.register(dialexPlugin, options)`                | `request.locale`, `request.getDictionary`               |
| [Koa](#koa)             | `dialexjs/koa`       | `app.use(dialexKoa(options))`                        | `ctx.locale`, `ctx.getDictionary`                       |
| [Hono](#hono)           | `dialexjs/hono`      | `app.use("*", dialexHono(options))`                  | `c.var.locale`, `c.var.getDictionary`                   |
| [Elysia](#elysia)       | `dialexjs/elysia`    | `app.use(dialexElysia(options))`                     | `locale`, `getDictionary`, `t` in the context           |
| [h3](#h3)               | `dialexjs/h3`        | default export of a Nitro middleware file            | `event.context.locale`, `.getDictionary`, `.t`          |
| [Hapi](#hapi)           | `dialexjs/hapi`      | `server.register({ plugin: dialexPlugin, options })` | `request.locale`, `request.getDictionary`               |
| [AdonisJS](#adonisjs)   | `dialexjs/adonis`    | `router.use([() => import("#middleware/dialex")])`   | `ctx.locale`, `ctx.getDictionary`                       |
| [NestJS](#nestjs)       | `dialexjs/nestjs`    | `DialexModule.forRoot(options)`                      | `req.locale`, `req.getDictionary`, decorators           |
| [SvelteKit](#sveltekit) | `dialexjs/sveltekit` | `export const handle = dialexHandle(options)`        | `event.locals.locale`, `.getDictionary`, `.t`           |
| [Astro](#astro)         | `dialexjs/astro`     | `export const onRequest = dialexAstro(options)`      | `Astro.locals.locale`, `.getDictionary`, `.t`           |
| [tRPC](#trpc)           | `dialexjs/trpc`      | spread into `createContext`                          | `ctx.locale`, `ctx.getDictionary`, `ctx.t`              |
| [Fetch API](#fetch-api) | `dialexjs/web`       | `createDialexHandler(options)(request)`              | `locale`, `getDictionary`, `t`, `headers`               |

## Express

```ts
import { dialexExpress } from "dialexjs/express";

function dialex(options?: ExpressDialexOptions): RequestHandler; // also exported as dialexExpress
```

Register it before your routes. Cookies are read from `req.cookies` when `cookie-parser` is installed, otherwise from the `Cookie` header. Options: `ExpressDialexOptions` (locale detection options, `dictionaries`, `setHeader`).

## Fastify

```ts
import dialexPlugin from "dialexjs/fastify";

const dialexPlugin: FastifyPluginAsync<FastifyDialexOptions>; // default export and named export
```

Needs Fastify 4 or later. Options: `FastifyDialexOptions`.

## Koa

```ts
import { dialexKoa } from "dialexjs/koa";

function dialex(options?: KoaDialexOptions): Middleware; // also the default export and dialexKoa
```

Options: `KoaDialexOptions`.

## Hono

```ts
import { dialexHono } from "dialexjs/hono";

function dialex(options?: HonoDialexOptions): MiddlewareHandler; // also exported as dialexHono
```

Read the values with `c.var.locale` and `c.var.getDictionary("home")`. Options: `HonoDialexOptions`.

## Elysia

```ts
import { dialexElysia } from "dialexjs/elysia";

function dialex(options?: ElysiaDialexOptions): Elysia; // also the default export and dialexElysia
```

Adds `locale`, `getDictionary` and `t` through `derive`, so they are typed in every handler. Options: `ElysiaDialexOptions` (= `BaseAdapterOptions`).

## h3

```ts
import { dialexH3 } from "dialexjs/h3";

function dialex(options?: H3DialexOptions): EventHandler; // also the default export and dialexH3
```

For h3 1.x (Nitro 2, Nuxt 3 and 4 server routes). Options: `H3DialexOptions`.

## Hapi

```ts
import { dialexHapi } from "dialexjs/hapi";

const dialexPlugin: Plugin<HapiDialexOptions>; // also the default export and dialexHapi
```

Options: `HapiDialexOptions`. Decorates the request in `onRequest`.

## AdonisJS

```ts
import { createDialexMiddleware } from "dialexjs/adonis";

function createDialexMiddleware(options?: AdonisDialexOptions): MiddlewareClass; // also default and dialexAdonis
```

Returns a middleware **class** for AdonisJS 6 and later; export it as the default of a file in `app/middleware`. Options: `AdonisDialexOptions`.

## NestJS

```ts
import { DialexModule } from "dialexjs/nestjs";
```

| Export                               | Description                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `DialexModule.forRoot(options?)`     | A dynamic module. `NestDialexOptions` adds `isGlobal` (default `true`) to the locale detection options and `dictionaries` |
| `DialexModule.forRootAsync(options)` | Builds the options in `useFactory`, with `imports` and `inject` available. `NestDialexAsyncOptions`                       |
| `DialexService`                      | Injectable: `getDefaultLocale()`, `getSupportedLocales()`, `resolveLocale(req)`, `getDictionary(name, locale?)`           |
| `DialexMiddleware`                   | Sets `req.locale` and `req.getDictionary` and the `Content-Language` header                                               |
| `DialexInterceptor`                  | The same, as an interceptor                                                                                               |
| `@DialexLocale()`                    | Parameter decorator: the resolved locale                                                                                  |
| `@DialexDictionary(name)`            | Parameter decorator: the dictionary for the resolved locale                                                               |
| `DIALEX_OPTIONS`                     | The injection token of the options                                                                                        |

## SvelteKit

```ts
import { dialexHandle, LANG_PLACEHOLDER } from "dialexjs/sveltekit";

function dialexHandle(options?: SvelteKitDialexOptions): Handle; // also the default export
const LANG_PLACEHOLDER: "%dialex.lang%";
```

Sets `event.locals.locale`, `getDictionary` and `t`, and replaces `%dialex.lang%` in the rendered HTML with the locale, so `<html lang="%dialex.lang%">` in `src/app.html` is right. `Handle` is a local structural type that works with SvelteKit 2 and 3.

## Astro

```ts
import { dialexAstro } from "dialexjs/astro";

function dialex(options?: AstroDialexOptions): MiddlewareHandler; // also the default export and dialexAstro
```

Export it as `onRequest` from `src/middleware.ts`. Options: `AstroDialexOptions`.

## tRPC

```ts
import { createDialexContext } from "dialexjs/trpc";

function createDialexContext(
  options?: TrpcDialexOptions,
): (request: TrpcRequestLike) => TrpcDialexContext; // also default and dialexTrpc
```

`TrpcRequestLike` is a Fetch `Request`, or an object with `headers` and an optional `url`, which is what the fetch, Next.js, Express and standalone adapters pass to `createContext`. The result `{ locale, getDictionary, t }` belongs in your context.

## Fetch API

```ts
import createDialexHandler from "dialexjs/web";

function createDialexHandler(options?: WebDialexOptions): (request: Request) => Promise<WebDialex>;
```

For any runtime with a standard `Request` (React Router and Remix loaders, TanStack Start, SolidStart, Cloudflare Workers, Deno, Bun). `WebDialex` has `locale`, `getDictionary`, `t`, `headers` (`{ "Content-Language": ... }`, empty when `setHeader` is `false`) and `applyHeaders(response)`.

## `dialexjs/server`

```ts
import { createDialexServer } from "dialexjs/server";

function createDialexServer(source: DialexSource): DialexServer;

interface DialexServer {
  getDictionary<K extends DictionaryKey>(name: K, locale?: Locales): ResolveDictionaryType<K>;
  getT(locale?: Locales): Translate;
}
```

For code that is not tied to a request: Next.js Server Components, scripts, jobs. Create it once with the generated object:

```ts
// src/dialex.ts
import { dialex } from "./dialex.generated";
export const { getDictionary, getT } = createDialexServer(dialex);
```

`locale` defaults to the configured default locale, and a locale without content falls back along the [fallback chain](../guide/fallbacks.md). It needs the eager generated file: with `lazy` loading use the client entry points.


---

# File: api/testing.md

# Testing

Helpers for unit and component tests. They need no bundler plugin, config file or generated file, and they never touch cookies or `localStorage`, so tests cannot leak state into each other. See [Testing](../guide/testing.md) for worked examples.

## `dialexjs/testing`

### `createTestDialex(options)`

```ts
function createTestDialex(options: TestDialexOptions): TestDialex;
```

| Option          | Type                       | Default         | Description                                                                    |
| --------------- | -------------------------- | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `dictionaries`  | `DictionaryInput`          | —               | `defineDictionary` results, or a `{ name: { locale: content } }` map. Required |
| `locale`        | `string`                   | `defaultLocale` | The active locale                                                              |
| `defaultLocale` | `string`                   | `"en"`          | Fallback locale                                                                |
| `fallbacks`     | `Record<string, string[]>` | —               | Explicit [fallback chains](../guide/fallbacks.md)                              |

Returns a `TestDialex`:

| Member                | Description                                                       |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locale`              | The active locale                                                 |
| `getDictionary(name)` | The content of a dictionary for the active locale, with fallbacks |
| `t`                   | A [`t` function](./core.md#createt) for the active locale         |
| `withLocale(locale)`  | A new context over the same dictionaries under another locale     |

```ts
const dialex = createTestDialex({ dictionaries: [home], locale: "tr" });
expect(dialex.t("home.title")).toBe("Hoş Geldiniz");
expect(dialex.withLocale("en").getDictionary("home").title).toBe("Welcome");
```

### `mockRequest(url, options?)`

```ts
function mockRequest(url: string, options?: MockRequestOptions): Request;
```

Builds a standard `Request` that a server adapter resolves to `options.locale`. Relative URLs are resolved against `http://localhost`.

| Option    | Type                                        | Default    | Description                                                                                              |
| --------- | ------------------------------------------- | ---------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locale`  | `string`                                    | —          | The locale the request should resolve to                                                                 |
| `via`     | `"header" \| "cookie" \| "query" \| "path"` | `"header"` | How the locale is conveyed: `Accept-Language`, the `locale` cookie, `?locale=` or a leading path segment |
| `headers` | `Record<string, string>`                    | —          | More request headers                                                                                     |
| `cookies` | `Record<string, string>`                    | —          | More cookies                                                                                             |
| `method`  | `string`                                    | `"GET"`    | HTTP method                                                                                              |
| `body`    | `BodyInit \| null`                          | —          | Request body                                                                                             |

```ts
const res = await app.request(mockRequest("/dashboard", { locale: "tr", via: "cookie" }));
```

## `dialexjs/testing/react`

### `TestDialexProvider`

```tsx
function TestDialexProvider(props: TestDialexProviderProps): ReactElement;
```

`DialexProvider` for component tests: it renders `locale` immediately and never reads or writes cookies or `localStorage`. Give it the generated `dialex` export, or your own `dictionaries`.

| Prop                                | Type           | Description                                                |
| ----------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locale`                            | `string`       | The locale to render with. Default: the configured default |
| `dictionaries`, `config`, `loaders` | `DialexSource` | What the provider reads                                    |
| `children`                          | `ReactNode`    | The component under test                                   |

```tsx
import { dialex } from "../dialex.generated";

render(
  <TestDialexProvider {...dialex} locale="tr">
    <Header />
  </TestDialexProvider>,
);
```

## `dialexjs/testing/vue`

### `createTestDialex(locale?, source?)`

```ts
function createTestDialex(locale?: string, source?: DialexSource): VuePlugin;
```

A Vue plugin for component tests that starts in `locale` with no persistence. Pass the generated `dialex` export, or your own `dictionaries`, as `source`.

```ts
import { dialex } from "../dialex.generated";

mount(Header, { global: { plugins: [createTestDialex("tr", dialex)] } });
```
