- **`Cannot modify immutable headers`**: the response came from `fetch()` or `Response.redirect()`. `applyHeaders` copies such responses, so use its return value.
- **`[dialex] Dictionary "x" not found`**: the dictionary is not in `dialex.generated.ts`. Run `dx generate` and check that `include` in `dialex.config.ts` matches the file.


---

# File: guide/ai.md

# AI Assistants & MCP

Dialex is built to work seamlessly with AI coding assistants like Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, and Codex. It provides a dedicated Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, installable agent skills, machine-readable JSON output on all CLI commands, and automated setup.

## Setup with `dialex init`

When setting up Dialex in a new project, run:

```bash
dialex init --ai
```

This will automatically:

1. Install and register the Dialex MCP server in `.mcp.json`.
2. Add the Dialex skill definition to `.agents/skills/dialex/SKILL.md`.
3. Add key internationalization guidelines to `AGENTS.md`.

## MCP Server (`@dialexjs/mcp`)

The `@dialexjs/mcp` package runs over stdio and exposes tools that inspect dictionaries, check parity, and perform safe syntax-tree edits. It never executes project code and never calls paid translation APIs.

### Configuration

Add Dialex to your `.mcp.json`:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "dialex": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["@dialexjs/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Available Tools

| Tool                       | Type | Description                                                                  |
| -------------------------- | ---- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dialex_config`            | Read | Reads static configuration (`locales`, `defaultLocale`) without running code |
| `dialex_list_dictionaries` | Read | Lists all discovered dictionary files and their locales                      |
| `dialex_get_dictionary`    | Read | Returns translation leaf keys and values per locale                          |
| `dialex_check`             | Read | Runs parity and reference analysis, returning issues and annotations         |
| `dialex_find_usages`       | Read | Scans a file for dictionary calls (`getDictionary`, `t(...)`)                |
| `dialex_missing`           | Read | Lists keys that are missing or still contain `[TODO]` placeholders           |
| `dialex_set_key`           | Edit | Safely sets a string via AST; prevents overwriting unless `overwrite: true`  |
| `dialex_add_missing`       | Edit | Inserts missing keys across locales as `[TODO]` stubs                        |
| `dialex_generate`          | Tool | Regenerates `dialex.generated.ts` and `dialex-env.d.ts`                      |

### Documentation Resources

The server provides built-in markdown resources under `dialex://docs/<topic>`:

- `dialex://docs/guide`
- `dialex://docs/translate`
- `dialex://docs/icu`
- `dialex://docs/adapters`

## Agent Skills

Dialex publishes skills compatible with `skills` CLI:

```bash
npx skills add awaiden/dialex
```

Two skills are included:

- `dialex`: Core concepts, dictionary structure, and framework adapter patterns.
- `dialex-translate`: Workflow for detecting missing translations, inserting stubs, and verifying ICU parity.

## Machine-Readable JSON Output

All Dialex CLI commands accept `--json` for integration into automated pipelines and AI agents:

```bash
dialex check --json
dialex generate --json
dialex export --json
dialex import translations.json --json
dialex translate --dry-run --json
```

Output is emitted to stdout as structured JSON, while logs and warnings are suppressed. On error, the process exits with a non-zero code.


---

# File: guide/benchmarks.md

# Benchmarks

Numbers for the parts of an i18n library that run in your users' browsers and on your servers: how fast a message is formatted, and how many bytes the library adds to a bundle. They compare Dialex with [i18next](https://www.i18next.com), [intl-messageformat](https://formatjs.github.io) (the FormatJS core behind `react-intl`), [Lingui](https://lingui.dev), [Paraglide JS](https://paraglidejs.com) and [Intlayer](https://intlayer.org).

::: tip Read them as a guide, not a verdict
A micro-benchmark measures one thing on one machine. Your app's cost is usually somewhere else: rendering, network, data. Use these numbers to compare the libraries with each other, and run the benchmark on your own hardware before you rely on them.
:::

## What is measured

Four messages, formatted in English by every library, with the same values. Before anything is timed, the runner checks that all libraries return the same text.

| Case          | Message                                                       |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Lookup        | `Hello, world`                                                |
| Interpolation | `Hello, {name}!`                                              |
| Plural        | `{count, plural, =0 {No items} one {# item} other {# items}}` |
| Nested        | A `select` on `gender` that contains a `plural` on `count`    |

Each library is used the way its documentation recommends:

- **dialexjs**: `t("dictionary.key", values)` on ICU strings. `function messages` are TypeScript functions, `formatMessage` is the formatter on its own.
- **dialexjs dictionary object**: `getDictionary("home").title`, which returns the resolved dictionary. Only the lookup case applies, because a message with values goes through `t()`. `dictionary object` reads from a dictionary obtained once; `getDictionary per call` resolves the dictionary on every call.
- **i18next**: its own interpolation and plural keys (`items_one`, `items_other`). It has no inline `select`, so the nested case is not run.
- **intl-messageformat**: a formatter created once per message and reused. `no cache` creates it on every call, which is what happens when an app does not keep the instance.
- **@lingui/core**: messages compiled ahead of time, as `lingui compile` does.
- **Paraglide JS**: messages compiled to functions by `paraglide-js compile` (`m.plural({ count })`), in the default inlang message format.
- **Intlayer**: content declared in a `.content.ts` file and built by `intlayer build`. The dictionary is read once, as a component does with `useIntlayer`. `getIntlayer per call` reads it on every call.

## Throughput

Operations per second, higher is better. Median of 7 rounds of 400 ms after a 300 ms warm-up.

Dialex is green. Bars are drawn to scale inside one chart, so compare lengths within a chart, not between charts.

<BenchmarkChart metric="plural" title="Plural" subtitle="operations per second, higher is better" unsupported="not supported" />

<BenchmarkChart metric="nested" title="Nested select and plural" subtitle="operations per second, higher is better" unsupported="not supported" />

<BenchmarkChart metric="interpolation" title="Interpolation" subtitle="operations per second, higher is better" unsupported="not supported" />

<BenchmarkChart metric="lookup" title="Lookup" subtitle="operations per second, higher is better" unsupported="not supported" />

| Library                           |     Lookup | Interpolation |     Plural | Nested select and plural |
| --------------------------------- | ---------: | ------------: | ---------: | -----------------------: |
| dialexjs                          | 45,921,949 |    17,591,571 |  9,956,907 |                8,572,741 |
| dialexjs (function messages)      | 30,294,716 |    21,592,553 | 26,256,191 |               17,178,301 |
| dialexjs formatMessage            | 41,122,519 |    24,645,778 | 14,808,836 |               11,676,472 |
| dialexjs (dictionary object)      | 80,403,999 |           n/a |        n/a |                      n/a |
| dialexjs (getDictionary per call) | 77,900,218 |           n/a |        n/a |                      n/a |
| i18next                           |    391,482 |       315,556 |    200,486 |                      n/a |
| intl-messageformat                | 21,248,346 |     4,068,286 |    431,805 |                  394,363 |
| intl-messageformat (no cache)     |    220,735 |       165,743 |     22,636 |                   18,146 |
| @lingui/core                      |  7,628,934 |     5,609,820 |    271,897 |                  129,683 |
| Paraglide JS                      | 21,122,876 |    16,040,431 |     86,959 |                   91,792 |
| Intlayer                          | 64,030,320 |     2,126,902 |  1,351,726 |                1,228,197 |
| Intlayer (getIntlayer per call)   |    351,302 |       281,777 |    262,436 |                  252,884 |

Measured with Node v24.21.0 on an Intel Core i5-11400H, Linux x64, on 2026-10-13.

## Bundle size

The smallest useful program in each library: create it, load one plural message and format it. Bundled for the browser with esbuild and minified.

<BenchmarkChart metric="size" title="Bundle size" subtitle="gzip bytes, lower is better" />

| Program                      | Minified |     Gzip |   Brotli |
| ---------------------------- | -------: | -------: | -------: |
| dialexjs (t)                 |  8,025 B |  3,029 B |  2,760 B |
| dialexjs/icu (formatMessage) |  7,060 B |  2,619 B |  2,397 B |
| dialexjs (function messages) |  8,066 B |  3,052 B |  2,772 B |
| i18next                      | 43,721 B | 14,080 B | 12,762 B |
| intl-messageformat           | 33,567 B |  9,908 B |  8,883 B |
| Paraglide JS                 | 10,702 B |  3,952 B |  3,528 B |
| @lingui/core                 |  4,824 B |  2,087 B |  1,869 B |
| Intlayer                     | 17,207 B |  4,901 B |  4,381 B |

Versions: dialexjs 0.9.1, i18next 26.4.4, intl-messageformat 12.1.3, @lingui/core 6.9.1, @inlang/paraglide-js 2.27.0, intlayer 9.7.0, vite-intlayer 9.7.0.

## How to read these numbers

- **Plurals and numbers are where libraries differ.** A plural needs a `PluralRules` and a number formatter. Creating those on every call is slow, so Dialex keeps one per locale and options. Without it the plural case measured about 36,000 operations per second; with it, about 700,000, and about 9,900,000 once the category and the formatted number of a small count are remembered per locale.
- **Function messages skip the parser.** A message written as a TypeScript function is compiled by TypeScript, so plural and select cost the same as a template string.
- **`t()` does a little more than the formatter.** `dialexjs` splits the dotted path and looks the key up before it formats, which is why `formatMessage` alone is faster once values are formatted. A plain string without values is returned as it is, so `t()` is faster on lookup.
- **i18next does more per call.** It resolves fallback chains, namespaces and plugins on every `t()`, which is the feature set you pay for. The ICU plugin changes its numbers; this benchmark runs it without one.
- **Paraglide JS is the fastest other library at interpolation.** A message with a value is compiled to a template string. Its plural code creates a new `Intl.PluralRules` on every call (version 2.27.0), which is the cost Dialex removed, so plural is much slower than its interpolation (about 87,000 against 16 million operations per second).
- **Intlayer's lookup is a property read.** A plain string needs no work, which is why it is far ahead of every library that looks a path up or formats. Interpolation, plural and select go through node functions, and reading the dictionary on every call is much slower than reading it once. Reading a Dialex dictionary object is the same operation and lands in the same order of magnitude; with values, `t()` and Intlayer's node functions do real work, and that is where the columns differ.
- **Size is for the runtime only.** Lingui's figure is for messages compiled ahead of time, and does not include its `lingui` toolchain. Dialex ships its parser in the runtime, so ICU strings work without a compile step. The closures and caches that make formatting faster cost about 2 KB minified (0.7 KB gzip) over the interpreter they replaced.
- **Paraglide JS and Intlayer are measured with their own build tools.** Paraglide's figure is one compiled message plus its runtime. Intlayer needs its bundler plugin to run in a browser, so it is built with `vite-intlayer` and `vanilla-intlayer`.

## Run it yourself

The benchmark lives in `apps/benchmarks`. Build the packages once, then run:

```bash
bun run build:packages
bun run --cwd apps/benchmarks bench     # throughput
bun run --cwd apps/benchmarks size      # bundle size
```

Results are written to `apps/benchmarks/results/` as JSON, with the Node version and CPU they were measured on.


---

# File: guide/best-practices.md

# Best practices

These recommendations apply to every framework. Each one comes from how Dialex works: the dictionaries are compiled into `dialex.generated.ts`, the locale is resolved once per request or per app, and the types come from your dictionaries.

## Organize dictionaries

- Keep one dictionary per feature or page, next to the code that uses it (`checkout.content.ts` beside the checkout page). Small files are easy to review, to translate and to load lazily.
- Put text that is shared across the app in a `common` dictionary and keep everything else out of it, so it does not grow into a catch-all.
- Give every dictionary the same locales. `dx check` reports the keys and locales that are missing, and the editor extensions show them as you type.

## Name keys by meaning

A key says what the text is for, not what it currently says. When the wording changes, the key and every call site stay the same.

```ts
// Good: the key describes the role
defineDictionary("checkout", {
  en: { payButton: "Pay now", emptyCart: "Your cart is empty" },
  tr: { payButton: "Şimdi öde", emptyCart: "Sepetiniz boş" },
});

// Avoid: the key repeats the English text, and breaks when the text changes
defineDictionary("checkout", {
  en: { payNow: "Pay now", yourCartIsEmpty: "Your cart is empty" },
});
```

Group related keys under an object (`nav.about`, `nav.contact`) and keep the nesting shallow, two or three levels. Deeper trees are hard to read in `t("...")` calls.

## Write messages translators can finish

- Use [ICU messages](./icu.md) for plurals, selects and numbers: `{count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}`. Never build a sentence from pieces (`"You have " + n + " items"`), because word order and plural forms differ between languages.
- Prefer ICU strings to function values for text that goes to translators. Functions are fine for logic that only developers touch, but translation tools and `dx check` can validate an ICU string and cannot look inside a function.
- Keep placeholders the same in every locale. `dx check` reports a locale whose arguments differ from the others.

```ts
defineDictionary("cart", {
  en: { items: "{count, plural, =0 {Your cart is empty} one {# item} other {# items}}" },
  tr: { items: "{count, plural, =0 {Sepetiniz boş} other {# ürün}}" },
});

t("cart.items", { count: 3 }); // "3 items"; `count` is checked at compile time
```

## Keep the generated file current

- Commit `dialex.generated.ts` and `dialex-env.d.ts`. The app imports them, and a fresh checkout should build without a generate step.
- While developing, keep it fresh with `dx generate --watch`, or use the VS Code or Zed extension, which regenerate it for you when a dictionary changes.
- In CI, run `dx check --fail-on-stale`. It fails when the committed generated file no longer matches the dictionaries, when keys or locales are missing, and when translations are out of date.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
- run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
- run: bunx dx check --fail-on-stale
```

## Resolve the locale in one place

- Decide the locale once per request (on the server) or once per app (in the browser), and pass it down. Do not read cookies or `navigator.language` in individual components.
- With server rendering, give the client the locale the server used (`initialLocale`) so the first client render matches the HTML. Otherwise the page flashes the wrong language or hydration reports a mismatch.
- Set `<html lang>` to the active locale. The React, Preact, Svelte, Solid, Qwik and Lit providers do it for you; on the server, write it into the HTML you render.
- Remember the visitor's choice in the `locale` cookie, which the server adapters read, rather than in `localStorage`, which the server cannot see.

## Load only what a page needs

- Small apps do not need lazy loading: all dictionaries in one bundle is simplest and fastest. Turn it on when the dictionaries are a noticeable part of the bundle.
- With `lazy: "locale"`, a visitor downloads only the dictionaries of the page they open, in the language they use. See [Lazy Loading](./lazy-loading.md).
- Preload what the next navigation needs (`preloadDictionaries(dialex, "checkout")`) so the page does not wait for a download.

## Translate with a review step

- `dx translate` fills missing keys with `[TODO]` placeholders or machine translations. Treat its output like any other change: review the diff before merging.
- Commit `dialex.lock.json`. It records which source text each translation was made from, so `dx check` and `dx translate --stale` can tell when English changed and the translation did not.
- Search for `[TODO]` before a release. `dx check` reports every placeholder that is still there.

## Test with the real dictionaries

- Render components with the same `dialex` export the app uses, and assert on the text of one locale. [Testing](./testing.md) has wrappers for React and Vue.
- Test at least the default locale and one other, so a missing key or a plural form shows up in the test run and not in production.

## Work with your editor

- Install the [VS Code extension](./vscode.md), or [Zed and other editors](./zed.md) through the language server. You get diagnostics, hover, go to definition, completion and quick fixes for keys.
- Store a dictionary in a variable (`const home = useDictionary("home")`) and the editor still resolves `home.title`.
- Keep generated and build output out of the scan: Dialex already respects `.gitignore`, and `exclude` in `dialex.config.ts` covers the rest.

## Checklist

| Before you ship                          | Command or setting                         |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| Dictionaries and generated file agree    | `dx check --fail-on-stale`                 |
| No missing keys or locales               | `dx check`                                 |
| No leftover placeholders                 | `[TODO]`                                   |
| Translations match the source text       | `dx translate --stale`, `dialex.lock.json` |
| `<html lang>` follows the locale         | provider or server markup                  |
| Bundle contains only needed dictionaries | `lazy: "locale"`                           |


---

# File: guide/changelog.md

# Changelog

What changed in each release of `dialexjs`, `@dialexjs/cli`, `@dialexjs/mcp` and the VS Code extension. The notes are written in English. Every release also appears on [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/awaiden/dialex/releases).

All notable changes to Dialex are listed here. `dialexjs`, `@dialexjs/cli`, `@dialexjs/mcp` and the VS Code extension share one version number.

Releases after 0.4.0 are listed first and come from each release's changesets. The older ones below follow [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/). The project uses [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/).

## 0.9.1

No changes in this release.

## 0.9.0

### Minor Changes

- 4b70e2e: Add `@dialexjs/eslint-plugin`, ESLint and oxlint rules for unknown dictionaries and keys, dynamic keys, hard-coded text and dictionary files.

  Checks are configured once in `dialex.config.ts` under `lint.rules` (level and options per diagnostic code), and `dialex check`, the editors and the plugin all read it. The analyzer skips comments, understands dictionaries registered inline with `dictionaries: { name: ... }`, and honours `dialex-ignore` / `dialex-ignore-next-line` comments. `@dialexjs/cli/api` gains `analyzeProjectSync`, and editors get a `dialex.diagnostics` setting for use with the plugin.

## 0.8.0

### Minor Changes

- 621a03a: Seven new framework entry points and CLI support for them.

  - `dialexjs/preact`: Preact 10 and later. `<DialexProvider {...dialex}>`, `useDialex`, `useDictionary`, `useT`, `useDialexConfig`. No `preact/compat` needed.
  - `dialexjs/qwik`: `createDialexQwik({ ...dialex })` returns `useDialexProvider`, `useDialex`, `setLocale`, `useDictionary` (an accessor, `home().title`), `useT` and `getPersistedLocale`. Dictionaries stay in their module; only the locale is serialized into the page.
  - `dialexjs/lit`: `createDialex({ ...dialex })` holds the locale, and `DialexController` is a reactive controller that re-renders a Lit element on locale changes. It also works with plain custom elements through `subscribe`.
  - `dialexjs/react-native`: `DialexProvider` for React Native and Expo with `deviceLocales` (the device's languages) and `storage` (AsyncStorage, MMKV, anything with `getItem` and `setItem`). It uses the hooks of `dialexjs/react`.
  - `dialexjs/hapi`: the `dialexPlugin` for Hapi 21, adding `request.locale` and `request.getDictionary(name)`.
  - `dialexjs/adonis`: `createDialexMiddleware({ ...dialex })` for AdonisJS 6 and later, adding `ctx.locale` and `ctx.getDictionary(name)`.
  - `dialexjs/trpc`: `createDialexContext({ ...dialex })` puts the locale and dictionaries into the tRPC context from a Fetch `Request` or Node-style headers.
  - `DialexProvider` of `dialexjs/react` accepts `onLocaleChange(locale)`.
  - The `react` peer dependency is `>=19.0.0` (was `^19.3.0`), so Expo SDK apps pinned to React 19.2 install without a warning.
  - `dialex init` and the type registry detect Preact, Qwik, Lit, React Native / Expo, Hapi, AdonisJS and tRPC. React Native shares the `dialexjs/react` declarations.
  - `dialexjs/react-native` reads `storage` before it renders, so the first screen is already in the remembered language and a restore is not reported through `onLocaleChange`.
  - `dialexjs/qwik` loads lazy dictionaries (`lazy: true`) and renders the readers again when they arrive.
  - `dx generate` follows a `tsconfig.json` that extends a package (such as `@adonisjs/tsconfig`), or lists several configs, when it decides whether generated imports need the `.js` extension.
  - New examples: `examples/preact`, `qwik`, `lit`, `expo`, `hapi`, `adonis` and `trpc`.

  Documentation: a page for each new framework in five languages.

- 5c72368: Two new framework entry points and CLI support for four more frameworks.

  - `dialexjs/svelte`: Svelte 4 and 5 (plain Vite apps, and SvelteKit components). `provideDialex({ ...dialex })` in the root component, then `useDictionary("home")` and `useT("home")` return stores (`$home.title`, `$t("home.cart.items", { count })`). It uses `svelte/store` and Svelte's context, so no runes or compile step are needed.
  - `dialexjs/solid`: SolidJS. `<DialexProvider {...dialex}>` and `useDictionary("home")` returning an accessor (`home().title`), `useT`, `useDialex`.
  - `dialex init` and the type registry detect Svelte, Solid and React Router (framework mode), and `dialex-env.d.ts` augments `dialexjs/svelte` and `dialexjs/solid`.
  - New config option `output`: where `dialex generate` writes `dialex.generated.ts` (the type declarations go next to it). React Router apps keep their source in `app/`.
  - New examples: `examples/vue`, `examples/svelte`, `examples/solid` and `examples/react-router`.

  Documentation: new pages for Svelte, Solid and React Router, a Best practices guide, and Best practices and Troubleshooting sections on every framework page, in five languages.

### Patch Changes

- 6aa75d3: Documentation and editor hints.

  - **Every public export has a TSDoc comment**, so editors show what `defineDictionary`, `defineConfig`, the formatters, the adapter options and the framework contexts do on hover. A test fails when a new export has none.
  - **`dialex translate --json` no longer prints the parsed dictionaries.** The `pending` list carried the whole syntax tree of each dictionary; it now has `file`, `locale`, `key`, `source` (and `stale` or `translated` when they apply).
  - **Docs:** a full API reference (signatures, parameters, return values, failures and examples for every export), plus new pages for how Dialex works, requirements and peer ranges, a diagnostics reference with the JSON shape of `check`, troubleshooting, an FAQ, a glossary, and migration guides from i18next, react-intl, next-intl and vue-i18n. The CLI pages now document `--json`, exit codes, `--ai`, and `dialex lock`. A guard checks that the API reference names every export. All pages are available in English, Turkish, Spanish, German and Simplified Chinese.

- 71b5b3a: A second round of speed-ups.

  - **Plural messages are about 7 times faster.** The results of `Intl.PluralRules.select` and of the `#` number format for counts 0 to 255 are remembered per locale (exactly what Intl returned, so every locale and numbering system stays correct), and messages with two or three parts get unrolled closures. `t()` on a plural: 1.3 M to 9.9 M operations per second; nested select and plural: 1.2 M to 8.5 M; interpolation: 12.2 M to 16.9 M; lookup: 43.5 M to 46.3 M.
  - **Bundle size:** the `t` program is 8,025 B minified (3,029 B gzip), up from 7,227 B (2,739 B). The compiled closures and caches are the price of the speed above; the 10% size target was not met.
  - **Language server re-analysis is about 4 times faster.** After one edit in a project of 1,000 dictionaries it takes about 20 ms instead of about 75 ms: unchanged dictionaries and source files are reused, the tree is not walked again for a content edit, and unchanged diagnostics are not sent again.

- f5cc8bd: Faster message formatting. ICU messages and the `plural`, `number`, `date`, `relativeTime` and `list` helpers reuse one `Intl` formatter per locale and options instead of creating a new one on every call, and each message is compiled once into a closure instead of walked on every call.

  Measured with the new `apps/benchmarks` (operations per second, `t()` on ICU strings):

  | Case          | Before |  After |
  | ------------- | -----: | -----: |
  | Lookup        |  6.8 M | 43.5 M |
  | Interpolation |  4.0 M | 12.2 M |
  | Plural        | 0.70 M | 1.31 M |
  | Nested        | 0.65 M | 1.22 M |

  The plural case was about 36,000 operations per second before the shared formatters (the "Before" column above already includes them). The runtime got larger by about 19% (`t` program: 6,081 B to 7,227 B minified, 2,301 B to 2,739 B gzip) because of the compiler.

  Documentation: new Benchmarks and Comparison pages, in five languages.

## 0.7.2

### Patch Changes

- 0800399: Editor features follow a dictionary held in a variable: after `const s = useDictionary("showcase")`, hover, go to definition and completion work on `s.nav.features` and `s.`, in the language server and the VS Code extension.

## 0.7.1

### Patch Changes

- b883a78: The VS Code extension re-reads only the files that changed. `analyzeProject` takes an optional `cache` (`createAnalysisCache()`) that remembers parsed dictionaries and scanned source files by modification time, and the extension keeps the project layout and `.gitignore` rules until files are added or removed. On a synthetic project with 10,000 source files a refresh went from about 950 ms to about 240 ms.
- 8ee86f2: New package `@dialexjs/language-server`: a language server (LSP) for Dialex translations, so editors other than VS Code get diagnostics, hover, go to definition, completion, quick fixes and automatic `dialex.generated.ts` updates. The editor-independent features (hover, definition, completion, quick fixes, project discovery) moved into it and are shared with the VS Code extension.

## 0.7.0

### Minor Changes

- 5d7f143: The scanners (`dx generate`, `dx check`, the watcher, the analysis API and the VS Code extension) now respect `.gitignore`: files in ignored folders are no longer picked up as dictionaries or sources. Monorepo packages inherit the repository's `.gitignore`, and nested `.gitignore` files apply to their folder.

  New config option `exclude` (globs relative to the project) for anything else. All scanners now share one list of built-in ignores (`node_modules`, `dist`, `.next`, `dialex.locales`, and for sources `.nuxt`, `.output`, `.svelte-kit`, `.astro`, `coverage`, `*.d.ts`, generated and config files), so they no longer disagree.

### Patch Changes

- 3909e30: Fix the VS Code extension: the `.vsix` shipped without the `jiti` and runtime chunks that `extension.cjs` loads, so the extension failed to activate and its commands were "not found". Existing installs need the new `.vsix` from the GitHub Release.

## 0.6.0

### Minor Changes

- 725a0c0: The server adapters (Express, Fastify, Hono, Koa, Elysia, h3, Astro, SvelteKit, NestJS, Fetch API, Angular) accept the generated `config`, so `{ ...dialex }` from `dialex.generated.ts` is all they need: `defaultLocale`, `locales` and `fallbacks` no longer have to be repeated by hand. Explicit options still win.

  Express, Hono, Koa, Elysia, h3 and Astro also export `dialexExpress`, `dialexHono`, `dialexKoa`, `dialexElysia`, `dialexH3` and `dialexAstro`, so the adapter and the generated `dialex` object do not share a name. `dialex` keeps working.

- 39eca0b: `dialexjs` no longer depends on `fast-glob` and `unconfig` (about 2.9 MB of installed size, mostly `jiti`). The project scanner moved into `@dialexjs/cli`, which already did all the scanning.

  **Breaking:** the `dialexjs/scanner` entry point is gone, and adapters no longer scan the project at startup when no `dictionaries` are passed. Pass the generated registry (`{ ...dialex }` from `dialex.generated.ts`); an adapter without it only finds dictionaries already registered through `defineDictionary`.

## 0.5.2

### Patch Changes

- d5d3669: Add `localeFromPath` and `isLocale` to `dialexjs/routing`.

## 0.5.1

### Patch Changes

- 9b108bb: `@dialexjs/mcp` now uses zod 4 and the current MCP SDK (1.32).
- d1dcad5: Tested with Next.js 16. Next.js 16 calls the `middleware.ts` file `proxy.ts`; `createDialexMiddleware` works in either.

## 0.5.0

### Minor Changes

- 4050d36: `lazy: "locale"` splits dictionaries per locale, so a visitor only downloads the language they read. `dx generate` writes one module per dictionary and locale into a `dialex.locales/` folder next to `dialex.generated.ts`, and `loaders` points at them. In a real Vite build the main bundle holds neither language, and a Turkish page fetched only the `.tr` chunks until the visitor switched to English, which then fetched the `.en` ones.

  - Switching language downloads the new locale on demand. In React the current language stays on screen until the new one has arrived (the update runs in a transition); in Vue the dictionary is empty until it loads, and server-side rendering waits for it.
  - `preloadDictionaries(dialex, { locale: "tr" }, "pricing")` fetches a locale ahead of time.
  - A dictionary is split only when each locale is self-contained. If a locale uses something defined elsewhere in its file (an import or a helper), the dictionary is loaded whole and `dx generate` says why.
  - `dx check` reports missing or out-of-date per-locale modules, and `--fix` rewrites them. `lazy: true` is unchanged.
  - `dx generate` no longer treats its own output (`dialex.generated.ts`, `*.d.ts`) as dictionaries when `include` is broad, such as `src/**/*.ts`.

- b39c7f6: Stale translations are detected. `dx translate` now writes `dialex.lock.json`, which records a short hash of the source text behind each translation, so a later edit of the source no longer leaves the other languages silently out of date.

  - `dx check` warns about each translation whose source text changed since it was recorded (`stale-translation`), and `--fail-on-stale` makes it an error. The VS Code extension shows the same warning. Translations without a record (hand-written ones) are never reported.
  - `dx translate --stale` translates the out-of-date strings again; only these may replace an existing translation.
  - `dx lock` records the translations you already have, so existing projects can adopt the lock file (`--all` also accepts out-of-date ones). `dx import` records what it imports once a lock file exists.
  - MCP: `dialex_missing` also lists `stale` translations.

- 5235a9f: `t()` checks ICU arguments. `dx generate` writes `MessageArguments` into `dialex-env.d.ts` (read from each dictionary's default locale), so `t("cart.items", { count })` fails to compile when `count` is missing, misspelled or not a number. `plural`, `selectordinal` and `number` are `number`, `date` and `time` are `Date | number`, `select` is the union of its options, and a plain `{name}` takes a string, number, boolean or `Date`.

  A message that has ICU arguments can no longer be called without values (`t("cart.owner")` was allowed and returned the raw string). Pass the values, or remove the braces if they were literal.

  Adapters that scan the project at runtime (no `dictionaries` passed) no longer write `dialex-env.d.ts`; it was a second writer that could undo the generated file. Run `dx generate`.

## [0.4.0] - 2026-10-09

### Changed

- **Breaking:** the virtual modules (`virtual:dialex-dictionaries`, `virtual:dialex-config`) and the bundler plugins that provided them are gone. Dictionaries and config now come from `dialex.generated.ts`, which `dx generate` writes, so Dialex works with any bundler, `dialexjs/react` loads in plain Node (the cause of the SSR failures on TanStack Start), and tests need no stubs. Keep the file current with `dx generate --watch` in a second terminal, the VS Code extension (regenerates on save), or a script that runs before `dev` and `build`.

  | Before                                                         | After                                                                             |
  | -------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `dialexPlugin()` from `dialexjs/vite` in `vite.config.ts`      | Remove it. Run `dx generate`                                                      |
  | `withDialex(nextConfig)` from `dialexjs/next`                  | Remove it. `dialexjs/next` is gone; `next/middleware` and `next/link` stay        |
  | `<DialexProvider>`                                             | `<DialexProvider {...dialex}>` with `import { dialex } from "./dialex.generated"` |
  | `createDialex({ defaultLocale })` (Vue)                        | `createDialex({ ...dialex, defaultLocale })`                                      |
  | `getDictionary`, `getT` from `dialexjs/server`                 | `export const { getDictionary, getT } = createDialexServer(dialex)`               |
  | `preloadDictionaries("pricing")`                               | `preloadDictionaries(dialex, "pricing")`                                          |
  | `TestDialexProvider locale="tr"`, `createTestDialex("tr")`     | `<TestDialexProvider {...dialex} locale="tr">`, `createTestDialex("tr", dialex)`  |
  | Nuxt: `dialex: { defaultLocale, locales }` in `nuxt.config.ts` | Put them in `dialex.config.ts`; the module reads `dialex.generated.ts`            |

  `vite` is no longer a peer dependency. In Next.js, render the provider from a `"use client"` file that imports the generated file, because dictionaries hold functions that cannot be passed from a Server Component.

- `DialexLink` reads its settings from the provider, so it must be rendered inside a `DialexProvider`.
- The build-time "dictionary is missing a configured locale" error is gone with the plugin; `dx check` reports it.
- With `lazy: true`, `dx generate` writes dynamic imports (a `loaders` export) instead of static ones. The generated `dictionaries` export is then empty, so server code needs an eager file.
- `dialex-env.d.ts` and `dialex.generated.ts` use the locales your dictionaries define when `locales` is not set in the config.

### Added

- `dx generate` works without a `dialex.config.*`: every default applies and `locales` come from your dictionaries. `dx init` creates the config file for every framework.
- `dialex.generated.ts` also exports `config` (a client-safe copy of your settings, without `translate`), `dialex` (`{ dictionaries, config }`) and, in lazy mode, `loaders`. It also exports `locales` (a readonly tuple, handy for a language switcher) and the matching `Locale` union type.
- `dx check` reports a generated file that is out of date, and `dx check --fix` rewrites it. The comparison ignores formatting, so a formatter may rewrite the generated files.
- VS Code: `dialex.autoGenerate` (on by default) regenerates the generated files when a dictionary or config file changes, in projects that already have one, without running your config. New command **Dialex: Regenerate dialex.generated.ts**.
- `createDialexServer(dialex)` in `dialexjs/server`, `useDialexConfig()` in `dialexjs/react`, and `DEFAULT_CONFIG`.
- `examples/tanstack`: a TanStack Start (React, SSR) app with server-side locale detection, ICU plurals and a language switch.

### Fixed

- `dx generate --watch` never regenerated anything: chokidar 4 and later no longer understand globs. It now watches the project and reacts to added, edited and removed dictionary files and to config changes.
- Server adapters (`web`, `hono`, `express`, `koa`, `fastify`, `elysia`, `astro`, `h3`, `nestjs`, `sveltekit`) imported the project scanner (`fast-glob`, `unconfig`, `node:fs`) even when you pass `dictionaries`, which pulled those packages into SSR bundles. The scanner now loads only when no `dictionaries` are given.

## [0.3.0] - 2026-10-09

### Changed

- **Breaking:** every public name that started with `I18n` or `i18n` now starts with `Dialex` or `dialex`. The old names are gone, with no aliases. Rename imports as follows:

  | Before                                                                           | After                                                                                    |
  | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
  | `I18nConfig`, `resolveI18nConfig`                                                | `DialexConfig`, `resolveDialexConfig`                                                    |
  | `i18n()` in `dialexjs/hono`, `express`, `koa`, `elysia`, `astro`, `h3`           | `dialex()`                                                                               |
  | `i18nPlugin` (`dialexjs/vite`, `dialexjs/fastify`), `withI18n` (`dialexjs/next`) | `dialexPlugin`, `withDialex`                                                             |
  | `I18nProvider`, `useI18n`, `createI18n`, `I18nLink`, `I18nContext` (Vue)         | `DialexProvider`, `useDialex`, `createDialex`, `DialexLink`, `DialexContext`             |
  | `I18nModule`, `I18nService`, `I18nInterceptor`, `I18nMiddleware`, `injectI18n`   | `DialexModule`, `DialexService`, `DialexInterceptor`, `DialexMiddleware`, `injectDialex` |
  | `i18nHandle` (`dialexjs/sveltekit`), `resolveI18n` (`dialexjs/web`)              | `dialexHandle`, `resolveDialex`                                                          |
  | `createTestI18n`, `TestI18nProvider` (`dialexjs/testing`)                        | `createTestDialex`, `TestDialexProvider`                                                 |
  | Option types such as `HonoI18nOptions`, `NestI18nOptions`, `NuxtI18nOptions`     | `HonoDialexOptions`, `NestDialexOptions`, `NuxtDialexOptions`                            |

  Anything else with `I18n` in its name follows the same rule. A project that still has `i18n.config.ts` keeps working.

- `dialex export` writes to `dialex-export` by default instead of `i18n-export`.

### Added

- `dialex init` adds `dialexjs` and `@dialexjs/cli` to `package.json` (at the CLI's own version; packages you already list are left alone) and tells you which install command to run.

## [0.2.3] - 2026-10-09

### Changed

- `dialex init --ai` writes the skill to `.agents/skills/dialex/SKILL.md`, the agent-neutral location, instead of `.claude/skills/`. Tools that only read `.claude/skills` (Claude Code) need a copy or symlink there; `npx skills add` can install it for them.

### Added

- This changelog, a Changelog page in the documentation (all five languages), and a GitHub Release for every version tag, created from the matching section of this file.

## [0.2.2] - 2026-10-09

### Added

- `dx` command, a shorter alias for `dialex`, handy in `package.json` scripts.

### Changed

- **Breaking:** `dialex generate` now writes `src/dialex.generated.ts` instead of `src/i18n.generated.ts`. Rename the file and update your `import dictionaries from "./dialex.generated.js"` lines.
- `dialex init` now adds a `dx:generate` script (running `dx generate`) instead of `i18n:generate`. Existing scripts are left alone.
- `dialex-env.d.ts` only augments the entry points your project uses (for example `dialexjs/express`, or `dialexjs/react` and `dialexjs/server` for Next.js), based on `package.json`. If nothing is recognised, every entry point is still augmented.

### Fixed

- `dialex-mcp` exited immediately when started through a symlink, which is how `npx @dialexjs/mcp` and `node_modules/.bin` start it.
- The docs named the binary `dialexjs`; it is `dialex`.

## [0.2.1] - 2026-10-09

### Fixed

- `@dialexjs/cli` and `@dialexjs/mcp` 0.2.0 depended on the previous `0.1.0` of their sibling packages, because the packing step read stale versions from `bun.lock`. `@dialexjs/mcp` could not start with a fresh install.

### Changed

- The release workflow now stops before publishing if the tag, the package versions and `bun.lock` disagree.

## [0.2.0] - 2026-10-08

### Added

- `@dialexjs/mcp`: an MCP server (`dialex-mcp`) with nine tools to read config, dictionaries and issues, find usages, and make safe edits. It never calls a translation provider.
- Agent skills for `npx skills add awaiden/dialex`: `dialex` and `dialex-translate`.
- `--json` on `generate`, `export`, `import` and `translate`, next to `check`.
- `dialex init --ai` writes the skill, an `.mcp.json` entry and an `AGENTS.md` snippet.
- `llms.txt` and `llms-full.txt` for the documentation site, and an "AI assistants & MCP" guide in all five languages.

### Known issues

- Fresh installs of `@dialexjs/mcp@0.2.0` fail to start. Use 0.2.1 or later.

## [0.1.0] - 2026-10-08

First release.

### Added

- `dialexjs`: type-safe dictionaries with `t("dictionary.key.path")`, ICU messages, fallbacks, routing helpers, lazy loading and a testing helper, with adapters for Next.js, React, Vue, Nuxt, Angular, Express, Fastify, Koa, Hono, Elysia, SvelteKit, Astro, NestJS, h3 and Fetch-API runtimes.
- `@dialexjs/cli`: `init`, `generate`, `check`, `export`, `import` and `translate`, plus a static programmatic API at `@dialexjs/cli/api`.
- Translation providers for Claude, OpenAI, Gemini and DeepL.
- A VS Code extension with diagnostics, hover, go to definition, completion and quick fixes.
- Documentation in English, Turkish, Spanish, German and Simplified Chinese.

# File: guide/comparison.md

# Comparison

How Dialex differs from the libraries it is most often compared with: [i18next](https://www.i18next.com), [FormatJS](https://formatjs.github.io) (`react-intl` and `intl-messageformat`), [Lingui](https://lingui.dev), [Paraglide JS](https://paraglidejs.com) and [Intlayer](https://intlayer.org). All of them are good libraries, and the right one depends on how your team writes and translates text.

For numbers on speed and size, see [Benchmarks](./benchmarks.md).

## At a glance

| Question             | Dialex                                      | i18next                              | FormatJS                            | Lingui                                                       |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Where the text lives | TypeScript dictionaries next to the code    | JSON resources, loaded by namespace  | Messages in the code, plus catalogs | Messages in the code, extracted to catalogs                  |
| Message syntax       | ICU MessageFormat, or a TypeScript function | Its own `{{value}}` and plural keys  | ICU MessageFormat                   | ICU MessageFormat                                            |
| Typed keys           | Generated from your dictionaries            | Through resource type declarations   | Message ids are strings             | No keys: the source text is the id                           |
| Typed ICU arguments  | Generated from each message                 | Not part of the key types            | Not by default                      | Values come from the template, so TypeScript checks them     |
| Missing translations | `dialex check` fails the build              | Reported at runtime, with fallbacks  | Reported through `onError`          | Counted by `lingui extract`; `lingui compile --strict` fails |
| Extraction step      | None: the dictionaries are the source       | Optional tooling                     | `formatjs extract`                  | `lingui extract`                                             |
| Translator hand-off  | JSON, CSV and XLIFF export and import       | JSON, with many services integrating | JSON, in several vendor formats     | PO and JSON catalogs                                         |
| Lazy loading         | Per dictionary or per locale, generated     | Backends and namespaces              | Your own dynamic imports            | Your own dynamic imports                                     |

The cells describe each library's documented defaults. Every one of them can be extended with plugins or your own code.

## Dialex and i18next

i18next is the most widely used i18n library for JavaScript, with a large ecosystem of backends, language detectors and framework bindings. It keeps translations as JSON resources and offers runtime features such as namespaces, fallbacks and plugins.

Dialex makes a different trade. Dictionaries are TypeScript, compiled into one typed registry, so a wrong key or a wrong argument is a type error, and a missing locale fails `dialex check` before you ship. There is no runtime resource loading to configure; with [lazy loading](./lazy-loading.md) a dictionary is a code-split module.

Choose i18next when you need its plugin ecosystem, backends that fetch translations at runtime, or a runtime that is not tied to TypeScript. Choose Dialex when you want the compiler to guard your text.

## Dialex and FormatJS

FormatJS is the reference implementation of ICU MessageFormat for JavaScript, and `react-intl` builds React components on it. Messages are defined in code with `defineMessages` or `formatMessage`, extracted with the `formatjs` CLI, and can be precompiled.

Dialex uses the same message syntax, so ICU messages carry over. The difference is the surrounding workflow: Dialex does not need an extraction step, because the dictionary is the source, and it generates types for keys and arguments. The runtime is also smaller, as shown in [Benchmarks](./benchmarks.md).

Choose FormatJS when you want the standard implementation and its React components, or when your translation process is built around `formatjs extract`.

## Dialex and Lingui

Lingui keeps the message in the source (`t` and `Trans` macros), extracts catalogs to PO or JSON, and compiles them into a small runtime. The result is a very small bundle and an authoring style where the English text is written in the component.

Dialex keeps the text in dictionaries instead, so a key names its purpose and every locale sits beside the others in the file. Both approaches use ICU MessageFormat.

Choose Lingui when you prefer writing messages inline and have a PO-based translation process. Choose Dialex when you prefer named keys, and want them checked by the type system.

## Paraglide JS and Intlayer at a glance

Two libraries that also work at build time, next to Dialex:

| Question             | Dialex                                      | Paraglide JS                                                | Intlayer                                                    |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| Where the text lives | TypeScript dictionaries next to the code    | JSON message files per locale                               | `.content` files next to the components                     |
| Message syntax       | ICU MessageFormat, or a TypeScript function | Inlang format; ICU MessageFormat 1 and i18next by plugin    | Its own nodes (`t`, `plural`, `enu`, `select`), or ICU      |
| Typed keys           | Generated from your dictionaries            | Each message is a generated function                        | Through a `Dictionary` type on each declaration             |
| Typed ICU arguments  | Generated from each message                 | Parameters of the generated functions are typed             | Not covered in its documentation                            |
| Missing translations | `dialex check` fails the build              | The inlang CLI checks translations in CI                    | `intlayer content test` checks for them                     |
| Extraction step      | None: the dictionaries are the source       | None: messages are written in the JSON files                | `intlayer extract` moves strings out of components          |
| Translator hand-off  | JSON, CSV and XLIFF export and import       | Fink editor for non-developers; import and export by plugin | CMS and editor, `fill` with AI, JSON and YAML files         |
| Lazy loading         | Per dictionary or per locale, generated     | Unused messages are dropped by the bundler                  | `importMode`: `static`, `dynamic` or `fetch` per dictionary |

## Dialex and Paraglide JS

[Paraglide JS](https://paraglidejs.com) is a compiler from the inlang project. Messages live in JSON files, and the compiler turns each one into a function (`m.greeting({ name })`) with typed parameters, so a bundler can drop the messages you do not use. The message format is pluggable: the default is the inlang format, and plugins add ICU MessageFormat 1 and i18next files.

Dialex also generates types from your messages, but it keeps the text of a feature together in one dictionary, with every locale side by side, and runs ICU strings in a small runtime. Paraglide's per-message functions give the finest tree-shaking; Dialex's [lazy loading](./lazy-loading.md) splits by dictionary or by locale.

Choose Paraglide JS when per-message tree-shaking matters most, or when you want the inlang editor tools. Choose Dialex when you prefer dictionaries grouped by feature, ICU strings and function messages in one file, and a parity check across locales.

## Dialex and Intlayer

[Intlayer](https://intlayer.org) declares content in `.content` files next to each component (TypeScript, JSON, YAML or Markdown), each with a `key`, and builds them into dictionaries. Around that it offers a CMS and an editor, `fill` to complete translations with AI, `extract` to move strings out of components, and `content test` to find missing translations.

Dialex also keeps text in `*.content.ts` files next to the code, but it stays a library and a command line tool: messages are plain ICU strings or functions, and the only service it talks to is the one you choose for `dialex translate`.

Choose Intlayer when you want an editor for non-developers, per-component content with its own node types, and AI fill built into the workflow. Choose Dialex when you want standard ICU MessageFormat and no hosted service.

## When Dialex is not the right fit

- You need to load or change translations at runtime from a service, without a deploy.
- Your translators work in a tool that only reads PO files, and you do not want a conversion step. Dialex exports JSON, CSV and XLIFF.
- Your project is plain JavaScript. The main value of Dialex is the types it generates.
- You depend on an ecosystem plugin that only i18next, FormatJS or Lingui provide.

## Moving to Dialex

- Keep your ICU messages as they are; the syntax is the same.
- Turn each namespace or catalog into one `defineDictionary` file, and let `dialex check` find the keys that differ between locales.
- Import existing translations with [`dialex import`](../cli/import.md) from JSON, CSV or XLIFF.

# File: guide/concepts.md

# How Dialex works

Dialex keeps your translations in TypeScript, turns them into one generated module and a set of type declarations before your app runs, and reads them back with plain object lookups. This page is the map: read it once, and the rest of the docs fall into place.

## The pipeline

```text
  src/home.content.ts            dialex generate              your app at runtime
  ┌────────────────────┐        ┌──────────────────┐        ┌───────────────────────┐
  │ defineDictionary(  │  ───►  │ dialex.generated │  ───►  │ adapter or provider   │
  │   "home", { en,tr })│        │   .ts            │        │ resolves the locale   │
  └────────────────────┘        │ dialex-env.d.ts  │        │ getDictionary / t()   │
        you write                └──────────────────┘        └───────────────────────┘
                                    CLI, build time              runtime, per request
```

1. **You write dictionaries.** One `*.content.ts` file per dictionary, next to the code that uses it, each a `defineDictionary("name", { en: {...}, tr: {...} })` call. See [Dictionaries](./dictionaries.md).
2. **`dialex generate` compiles them.** It reads the files from their syntax tree (it does not run your code), writes `dialex.generated.ts` (the dictionaries and a client-safe copy of your config) and `dialex-env.d.ts` (the types). See [`dialex generate`](../cli/generate.md).
3. **An adapter resolves the locale.** On a server it looks at the URL, query string, cookie and `Accept-Language`; in a UI framework a provider holds the active locale. See [Locale Detection](./locale-detection.md).
4. **Your code reads a dictionary.** `getDictionary("home").title`, `t("home.title")` or a hook. It is an object lookup, plus ICU formatting when you pass values.

Nothing scans the file system at runtime, and nothing is parsed twice: ICU messages are compiled once, on first use.

## What each piece is

| Piece             | What it is                                                                                          | Where it lives                          |
| ----------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- |
| Dictionary        | A named object that maps each locale to its content: strings, nested objects, functions             | `*.content.ts`                          |
| Key path          | The address of a value: `home.nav.about` is dictionary `home`, key `nav.about`                      | In `t("home.nav.about")`                |
| Config            | `defaultLocale`, `locales`, `fallbacks`, `lazy`, `translate`...                                     | `dialex.config.ts`                      |
| Generated module  | The dictionaries and settings, as one importable file                                               | `dialex.generated.ts` (do not edit)     |
| Type declarations | Augment `DictionaryRegistry` so names and paths autocomplete and are checked                        | `dialex-env.d.ts` (do not edit)         |
| Adapter           | Framework glue: resolves the locale and gives you `getDictionary` and `t`                           | `dialexjs/<framework>`                  |
| CLI               | `generate`, `check`, `export`, `import`, `translate`, `lock`, `init`                                | `@dialexjs/cli`                         |
| Editor tooling    | Diagnostics, hover, go to definition, completion and quick fixes, from the same analysis as `check` | VS Code extension, language server, Zed |

## What is decided when

| Decided at          | What                                                                                                                |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Write time          | Which keys exist, and what type each has                                                                            |
| `dialex generate`   | The generated module and the types. A change to a dictionary or the config is not seen until you run it again       |
| `dialex check` (CI) | Whether every locale has every key, whether ICU messages are valid and consistent, whether code refers to real keys |
| Request or render   | The locale, and so which content is read; ICU values are formatted here                                             |

Because the types come from the generated file, **forgetting to run `dialex generate` is the most common cause of "the types are wrong"**. Run `dialex generate --watch` while you develop, use the editor extension (it regenerates on save), and let `dialex check` fail CI when the file is stale.

## The three ways to say a message

| Form         | Example                                                  | Use it for                                                                             |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Plain string | `title: "Welcome"`                                       | Text without values                                                                    |
| ICU string   | `items: "{count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}"` | Values, plurals, selects, numbers and dates; works with translators' tools             |
| Function     | `` greeting: (name: string) => `Hello, ${name}!` ``      | Full TypeScript, including `plural()` and the other [formatters](../api/formatting.md) |

All three can sit in the same dictionary. See [ICU Messages](./icu.md) and [Formatting & Plurals](./formatting.md).

## Where to go next

- Start a project: [Getting Started](./getting-started.md), then your [framework](../frameworks/README.md).
- Look something up: the [API reference](../api/README.md) and the [CLI reference](../cli/README.md).
- Something does not work: [Troubleshooting](./troubleshooting.md).

# File: guide/configuration.md

# Configuration

Dialex loads `dialex.config.*` (or `i18n.config.*`) from the project root; `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, and `.json` are supported.

```ts
// dialex.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "dialexjs";

export default defineConfig({
  defaultLocale: "en",
  locales: ["en", "tr"],
  include: "**/*.content.ts",
});
```

| Option          | Type                          | Default             | Description                                                                                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `defaultLocale` | `string`                      | `"en"`              | Locale used when none can be resolved                                                                                                                                          |
| `locales`       | `string[]`                    | —                   | Supported locales; enables locale type narrowing and parity checks. When omitted, `dx generate` uses the locales your dictionaries define                                      |
| `include`       | `string \| string[]`          | `"**/*.content.ts"` | Glob(s) for dictionary files                                                                                                                                                   |
| `exclude`       | `string[]`                    | —                   | Globs, relative to the project, that are never scanned for dictionaries or sources                                                                                             |
| `output`        | `string`                      | —                   | Where `dialex generate` writes `dialex.generated.ts`, relative to the project; the type declarations go next to it. Defaults to `src/`, or the project root when there is none |
| `configFile`    | `string`                      | —                   | Custom config path                                                                                                                                                             |
| `fallbacks`     | `Record<string, string[]>`    | —                   | Explicit [fallback chains](./fallbacks.md) per locale                                                                                                                          |
| `prefixDefault` | `boolean`                     | `true`              | Whether the default locale also gets a URL prefix. Read by `DialexLink` and the [routing helpers](./routing.md)                                                                |
| `lazy`          | `boolean \| "locale"`         | `false`             | Load dictionaries on demand (client bundles): `true` splits per dictionary, `"locale"` per dictionary and locale. See [Lazy Loading](./lazy-loading.md)                        |
| `lint`          | `{ rules }`                   | —                   | Turn checks off or change their level and options, for `dialex check`, the editors and the [ESLint and oxlint rules](./linting.md)                                             |
| `translate`     | `{ provider, sourceLocale? }` | —                   | Provider for [`dialex translate`](../cli/translate.md)                                                                                                                         |

Dialex skips `node_modules`, build output and everything your `.gitignore` files ignore (including the repository's, for a package inside a monorepo). Use `exclude` for anything else, such as a vendored folder you do commit.

The file is optional: without it every default above applies. `dx generate` copies the settings the runtime needs (not `translate`) into `dialex.generated.ts`, so rerun it after changing the file.

## Where the file is found

The tools look in the project root (the folder you run `dialex` from, or the folder of the project in the editor) for `dialex.config.<ext>` and then `i18n.config.<ext>`, with `<ext>` one of `ts`, `mts`, `cts`, `js`, `mjs`, `cjs` or `json`. The first one found wins. `-c, --config <path>` (or the `dialex.configPath` editor setting) points at a different file. In a monorepo, each package that has a config is its own project, and a package with only dictionaries uses the defaults.

## How the tools read it

| Tool                                                        | Reads the config by                                                   |
| ----------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dialex generate`, `check`, `export`, `import`, `translate` | Running the file, so values can be computed (`locales: getLocales()`) |
| The editor extension and language server                    | Reading its syntax tree, and never running it                         |

A config made of literals (strings, arrays, booleans) is understood everywhere. A setting that is computed is invisible to the editor, which then uses the default for it and logs a note. If an editor must know `locales`, write them out.

## Examples

A project with regional fallbacks and the default locale served without a prefix:

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "dialexjs";

export default defineConfig({
  defaultLocale: "en",
  locales: ["en", "pt", "pt-BR", "es"],
  fallbacks: { "pt-BR": ["pt", "es"] },
  prefixDefault: false,
});
```

A framework whose source folder is not `src/`, with a vendored folder excluded:

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  defaultLocale: "en",
  locales: ["en", "tr"],
  output: "app/dialex.generated.ts",
  exclude: ["vendor/**"],
});
```

# File: guide/diagnostics.md

# Diagnostics reference

Every problem Dialex reports has a code, a severity and a message. The same checks run in [`dialex check`](../cli/check.md), in the [VS Code extension](./vscode.md) and in the [language server](./zed.md), so a problem looks the same everywhere.

## Severities

| Severity  | Meaning                                                  | In `dialex check`                                                                   | In the editor |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `error`   | Something is wrong and will fail at runtime or in review | Exit code `1`                                                                       | Error         |
| `warning` | Something is probably wrong or left unfinished           | Reported, exit code `0` (`--fail-on-stale` turns `stale-translation` into an error) | Warning       |
| `info`    | A file cannot be analyzed, which is not an error         | Not shown                                                                           | Information   |

`unused-key` and `unused-dictionary` are warnings in `check`; editors show them as faded-out text (a hint) so they do not clutter the Problems panel, and only when the `unusedKeys` setting is on.

## Dictionary files

| Code                 | Severity | Message                                                                                 | Meaning and fix                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| -------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invalid-dictionary` | error    | `Failed to parse dictionary: ...`                                                       | The file has a syntax error. Fix the syntax; the message says where                                                                                                                               |
| `invalid-dictionary` | error    | `Default export does not appear to be a valid defineDictionary output.`                 | Only with `runtime` analysis. `export default` must be `defineDictionary(...)`                                                                                                                    |
| `invalid-locale`     | error    | `Locale "x" content is empty or invalid.`                                               | Only with `runtime` analysis. A locale's content must be an object                                                                                                                                |
| `unanalyzable`       | info     | `This dictionary uses spreads, computed keys, imported values, or a computed name, ...` | The static tools cannot read the file. `dialex check` runs it instead; editors skip it. Use literal objects to get editor support (see [Dictionaries](./dictionaries.md#what-the-tools-can-read)) |
| `missing-locale`     | error    | `Missing configured locale "de"`                                                        | A locale in `locales` has no content in this dictionary. Add it, or run `dialex check --fix`                                                                                                      |
| `missing-key`        | error    | `Locale "tr" is missing key "nav.about"`                                                | Another locale has the key. Add it, run `--fix` (copies the value with a `[TODO]` marker) or use the editor's quick fix                                                                           |
| `todo-placeholder`   | warning  | `Locale "tr" key "title" still has a [TODO] placeholder`                                | A value still starts with `[TODO] `, left by `--fix`. Translate it, or run [`dialex translate`](../cli/translate.md)                                                                              |
| `stale-translation`  | warning  | `Locale "tr" key "title" is out of date: the "en" text changed after it was translated` | The source text changed after the translation was recorded in `dialex.lock.json`. Update the translation, then run `dialex lock`                                                                  |

## ICU messages

| Code                    | Severity | Message                                                                                                                      | Meaning and fix                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `invalid-icu`           | error    | `Invalid ICU message "a.items" (tr): ICU syntax error at 27: Missing required "other" option`                                | The string uses `plural`, `select`, `number`... and does not parse. The message gives the position. Plural and select need an `other` branch |
| `invalid-icu`           | warning  | `"a.soft" (en) contains braces but is not valid ICU, so t() values cannot be applied: ...`                                   | A string with plain braces does not parse, so `t()` would return it unchanged. Quote literal braces: `'{'`                                   |
| `icu-args-mismatch`     | error    | `Locale "tr" uses different arguments than "en" for "a.greeting" (expected name:any, found ad:any)`                          | Translations of one key must use the same argument names. Rename the argument in the translation                                             |
| `icu-plural-categories` | warning  | `Locale "ru" plural "count" in "a.items" has no "few", "many" option (used by this language; "other" will be shown instead)` | The language needs more plural categories than the message gives. Add them                                                                   |

## Source code

These need source files to scan; they are skipped when there are none. See [`dialex check`](../cli/check.md#what-it-checks) for what is scanned.

| Code                 | Severity | Message                              | Meaning and fix                                                                                                                            |
| -------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `unknown-dictionary` | error    | `Unknown dictionary "zzz"`           | `getDictionary("zzz")`, `useDictionary("zzz")` or `@DialexDictionary("zzz")` names a dictionary that does not exist                        |
| `unknown-path`       | error    | `Unknown translation path "a.nope"`  | `t("a.nope")` where `a` is a known dictionary but has no such key. The editor offers a quick fix that adds the key to every locale         |
| `unused-key`         | warning  | `Key "only_en" is possibly unused`   | No source file contains the key's last segment as a word. A heuristic: dynamic access is never reported, and some unused keys go unnoticed |
| `unused-dictionary`  | warning  | `Dictionary "c" is never referenced` | No source file contains the dictionary's name                                                                                              |

Comments are never checked. A dictionary registered in code with an object literal, `dictionaries: { name: ... }`, counts as known, so reading it with `getDictionary("name")` is not an error. To silence a reference that is fine, put `dialex-ignore-next-line` in a comment on the line above it, or `dialex-ignore` in a comment on the same line:

```ts
// dialex-ignore-next-line
const d = getDictionary("from-a-plugin");
```

For the same checks in ESLint and oxlint, see [Linting](./linting.md).

## Generated files

`dialex check` also compares `dialex.generated.ts` and `dialex-env.d.ts` with what `dialex generate` would write, ignoring formatting. This one has no code:

| Severity | Message                                                                                | Fix                   |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| error    | `Out of date with your dictionaries or config. Run `dx generate`(or`dx check --fix`).` | Run `dialex generate` |

## Output formats

**Human** output groups issues by file, with the line number after each message.

**`--json`** prints one object and nothing else:

```json
{
  "success": false,
  "diagnostics": [
    {
      "file": "src/features/a/a.content.ts",
      "name": "a",
      "errors": ["Missing configured locale \"de\""],
      "warnings": ["Key \"only_en\" is possibly unused"],
      "annotations": [
        { "level": "error", "message": "Missing configured locale \"de\"", "line": 3 }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "totalIssues": 1,
  "totalWarnings": 1,
  "fixed": 0
}
```

| Field           | Description                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `success`       | `false` when there is at least one error. The exit code is `1` in that case                                                                                                                            |
| `diagnostics`   | One entry per file with a problem: `file` (relative to the project), `name` (the dictionary, when it is one), `errors`, `warnings` and `annotations` (`level`, `message`, one-based `line` when known) |
| `totalIssues`   | The number of errors                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `totalWarnings` | The number of warnings                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `fixed`         | How many values `--fix` inserted                                                                                                                                                                       |

**`--github`** prints one workflow command per annotation (`::error file=...,line=...,title=dialex::message`), which GitHub shows on the files of a pull request.
