# File: guide/dictionaries.md

# Dictionaries

A dictionary is a named object mapping each locale to its content. Files are discovered by the `include` glob (default `**/*.content.ts`).

```ts
import { defineDictionary } from "dialexjs";

export default defineDictionary("home", {
  en: { title: "Hello" },
  tr: { title: "Merhaba" },
});
```

`defineDictionary` has two call forms:

```ts
defineDictionary("home", { en: {...}, tr: {...} });
defineDictionary({ name: "home", dictionary: { en: {...}, tr: {...} } });
```

Both return `{ name, dictionary }` and register the dictionary in the in-process `globalDictionaries` map.

## Values

Values can be strings, nested objects, or functions. Functions give you typed interpolation:

```ts
en: {
  greeting: (name: string) => `Hello, ${name}!`,
  items: (n: number) => (n === 1 ? "1 item" : `${n} items`),
}
```

## Locale parity

Every dictionary should define the same keys for every locale. Run [`dialex check`](../cli/check.md) in CI to enforce it; it also reports a configured locale that a dictionary lacks.

## Rules

- **The name is a literal and unique.** `defineDictionary("home", ...)`: a string literal, not a variable or an expression. It is the first segment of every [key path](./key-paths.md) and the argument of `getDictionary`. Two dictionaries with the same name collide: only one is reachable.
- **One default export per file.** `dialex generate` finds dictionaries by the `include` glob and reads the default export of each file.
- **Every locale has the same keys.** [`dialex check`](../cli/check.md) reports the ones that do not.
- **Keys cannot contain dots.** A dot is the separator of a key path, so `"nav.about"` is a nested `nav` object with an `about` key, not one key.

<a id="what-the-tools-can-read"></a>

## What the tools can read

`dialex generate`, `dialex check`, the editor extension and the language server read your dictionaries from their **syntax tree**, without running them. That is what makes them fast and safe to run in an editor. It also means they can only understand what is written as plain values:

| In the dictionary file                                             | Read statically? |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------- |
| `defineDictionary("home", { en: { ... }, tr: { ... } })`           | Yes              |
| `defineDictionary({ name: "home", dictionary: { ... } })`          | Yes              |
| Nested objects, string literals, functions and methods             | Yes              |
| `...shared` (a spread) anywhere in the locales or their content    | No               |
| Computed keys: `[key]: "..."`                                      | No               |
| A locale whose content is a variable or an import: `en: enStrings` | No               |
| A name that is not a string literal                                | No               |

A dictionary that cannot be read statically is not wrong; the tools just have to run it. `dialex check` does (it imports the file), and the editor reports the file as "not analyzable" and skips it, so it has no diagnostics, hover or completion for its keys. If you want editor support everywhere, keep dictionaries as literal objects, and share text with a function or a helper that is called inside a leaf instead of spreading objects.


---

# File: guide/fallbacks.md

# Locale Fallbacks

When a dictionary has no content for the requested locale, Dialex walks a fallback chain instead of jumping straight to the default:

1. the locale itself (`pt-BR`)
2. its explicit fallbacks from the config, in order
3. its subtag truncations (`pt-BR` → `pt`)
4. the truncations of the explicit fallbacks
5. `defaultLocale`

If nothing matches, the first locale defined in the dictionary is used.

```ts
// dialex.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from "dialexjs";

export default defineConfig({
  defaultLocale: "en",
  locales: ["en", "es", "pt"],
  fallbacks: {
    "pt-BR": ["pt", "es"],
    gl: ["es"],
  },
});
```

For example, a request for `tr-TR` with a Turkish dictionary resolves `tr` automatically, with no configuration. A request for `gl` with no Galician content resolves `es`.

A warning is logged whenever content comes from a different locale than the one requested.

## Adapters

Server adapters also accept `fallbacks` directly, which is useful when you pass `dictionaries` instead of relying on the config file:

```ts
app.use(dialex({ dictionaries, locales: ["en", "es"], fallbacks: { pt: ["es"] } }));
```

Fallbacks apply to dictionary lookups. [Locale detection](./locale-detection.md) still only returns locales listed in `locales`.


---

# File: guide/faq.md

# FAQ

Short answers, with links to the page that has the detail.

## Design

### Why are dictionaries TypeScript files and not JSON?

So the compiler can check them. A dictionary is code: its keys are typed, a value can be a function with typed parameters, and editors can jump from `t("home.title")` to the definition. JSON stays available at the edges: [`dialex export`](../cli/export.md) writes JSON, CSV or XLIFF for translators and [`dialex import`](../cli/import.md) writes their work back into the TypeScript files.

### Can I load translations from an API or a database at runtime?

Dialex is built for translations that ship with the app. A dictionary is any object, so you can fill one yourself and pass it as `dictionaries` to an adapter or provider, but then it is not typed, checked or generated for you. For content that changes without a deploy, use your CMS and keep UI strings in Dialex.

### How big is the runtime?

The `t()` function with the ICU parser and formatter is about 8 KB minified (3 KB gzip); `dialexjs/icu` on its own is about 7 KB. The framework adapters are small on top of that. See [Benchmarks](./benchmarks.md) for the measured figures and the comparison with other libraries.

### Does it work with server-side rendering?

Yes. The server adapters resolve the locale per request, and the UI providers take an `initialLocale` so the first client render matches the server's. A remembered locale is applied after mount, on purpose, so hydration never mismatches. See your [framework page](../frameworks/README.md).

## Locales

### How do I add a language?

1. Add it to `locales` in `dialex.config.ts`.
2. Run `dialex check --fix`: every dictionary gets the missing keys, copied from the default locale and marked `[TODO]`.
3. Translate them: by hand, with [`dialex translate`](../cli/translate.md) and a provider, or through [`export`/`import`](../cli/export.md).
4. Run `dialex generate` and `dialex check`.

### Does Dialex pick the language from the browser?

On the server, yes: adapters read `Accept-Language`, the URL, the query string and cookies, in that [order](./locale-detection.md). In the browser the providers do not read `navigator.language`: they use the locale the server resolved and the choice the user made (kept in a cookie or `localStorage`). React Native takes the device's languages through `deviceLocales`.

### What happens when a translation is missing?

The lookup follows the [fallback chain](./fallbacks.md): the locale itself, explicit `fallbacks`, the language without region (`pt-BR` to `pt`), then the default locale. If nothing has the key, `t()` warns and returns the path. `dialex check` reports missing keys so they do not reach production.

### Does it support right-to-left languages?

Dialex translates text and formats numbers and dates; it does not set the text direction. The providers keep `<html lang>` in sync with the locale. Derive `dir` from the locale yourself, for example `dir={["ar", "he", "fa"].includes(locale) ? "rtl" : "ltr"}`.

### How do plurals work in languages with many forms?

Messages use ICU `plural` and `selectordinal` with the CLDR rules of the locale, through `Intl.PluralRules`. Russian needs `one`, `few`, `many` and `other`; Arabic has six categories. `dialex check` warns when a message lacks a category its language needs. See [ICU Messages](./icu.md).

## Workflow

### Do I have to run `dialex generate` all the time?

Run `dialex generate --watch` while you develop, or use the [VS Code extension](./vscode.md), which regenerates on save. In CI, run `dialex check`: it fails when the generated files are out of date.

### Where should I commit the generated files?

Either way works. Committing them means a fresh clone type-checks without a build step; ignoring them means every install must run `dialex generate`. `dialex check` compares the generated files with what `generate` would write, so if you commit them, CI keeps them honest.

### How do translators work with it?

Give them [`dialex export`](../cli/export.md) output (JSON, CSV or XLIFF); they never see TypeScript. Bring their work back with [`dialex import`](../cli/import.md), which validates ICU messages and refuses unknown keys. Or let a provider translate with [`dialex translate`](../cli/translate.md), and use `dialex lock` to notice when a source text changes afterwards.

### Does `dialex translate` send my code anywhere?

No. Nothing is sent unless you configure a provider, and then only the strings to translate (not your code) go to that provider, in batches. `dialex translate --dry-run` lists what would be sent.

### Can I use it in a monorepo?

Yes. Each package with a `dialex.config.*` (or just `*.content.ts` files) is a project. The CLI works from the folder you run it in, and the editor tooling finds every project in the workspace and keeps nested projects apart. `.gitignore` files of the repository are respected.

## Tooling

### Why does the editor skip one of my dictionaries?

It cannot read it without running code: it uses a spread, a computed key, an imported value or a computed name. Use literal objects, or accept that `dialex check` (which evaluates the file) is the check for that file. See [Dictionaries](./dictionaries.md#what-the-tools-can-read).

### What does "pre-1.0" mean for me?

The API can change between minor versions. Breaking changes ship in a minor release, are listed in the [changelog](./changelog.md), and patch releases stay compatible. Pin the minor version you use.


---

# File: guide/formatting.md

# Formatting & Plurals

Dialex ships small, typed helpers built on `Intl`. They live in the `dialexjs` package and work anywhere dictionary functions run: server or client.

```ts
import { defineDictionary, plural, formatters } from "dialexjs";

const en = formatters("en");

export default defineDictionary("cart", {
  en: {
    items: (n: number) => plural("en", n, { one: "1 item", other: `${n} items` }),
    total: (amount: number) =>
      `Total: ${en.number(amount, { style: "currency", currency: "USD" })}`,
  },
  tr: {
    items: (n: number) => plural("tr", n, { other: `${n} ürün` }),
    total: (amount: number) =>
      `Toplam: ${formatters("tr").number(amount, { style: "currency", currency: "TRY" })}`,
  },
});
```

## Helpers

| Helper                                     | Built on                  | Notes                                                                    |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `plural(locale, count, forms)`             | `Intl.PluralRules`        | `other` is required; `zero`, `one`, `two`, `few`, `many` are optional    |
| `number(locale, value, options?)`          | `Intl.NumberFormat`       | Currency, percent, units, compact notation                               |
| `date(locale, value, options?)`            | `Intl.DateTimeFormat`     | Accepts `Date`, timestamp, or ISO string                                 |
| `relativeTime(locale, value, unit, opts?)` | `Intl.RelativeTimeFormat` | `relativeTime("en", -1, "day", { numeric: "auto" })` → `"yesterday"`     |
| `list(locale, values, options?)`           | `Intl.ListFormat`         | `list("en", ["a", "b", "c"])` → `"a, b, and c"`                          |
| `formatters(locale)`                       | all of the above          | Returns the helpers pre-bound to a locale, without the `locale` argument |

`plural` follows the CLDR rules for the locale, so English uses `one`/`other`, French treats 0 and 1 as `one`, and Russian and Arabic use `few`/`many` (and `zero`/`two` for Arabic). If a locale's category has no matching form, `other` is used.

For messages written as plain strings with `{count, plural, ...}`, see [ICU Messages](./icu.md).

The helpers take the locale as an explicit argument because each locale's content is written inside its own block of the dictionary.


---

# File: guide/getting-started.md

# Getting Started

Dialex is an i18n framework built around dictionaries defined in TypeScript. A compile step turns them into a static registry and type declarations, so runtime lookups are plain object access.

::: warning Pre-1.0
Dialex is below 1.0, so the API can still change between minor versions. Breaking changes are called out in the [changelog](./changelog.md) and ship in a minor release; patch releases stay compatible. Pin the minor version (`~0.8.0`) if you need a stable surface.
:::

## Packages

| Package         | Purpose                                                              |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `dialexjs`      | Core runtime and framework adapters                                  |
| `@dialexjs/cli` | `dialex` / `dx` binaries for scaffolding, codegen, and parity checks |

## Install

```bash
# bun
bun add dialexjs
bun add -d @dialexjs/cli

# npm
npm install dialexjs
npm install -D @dialexjs/cli

# pnpm
pnpm add dialexjs
pnpm add -D @dialexjs/cli
```

## Scaffold

```bash
dialex init
```

Or headless:

```bash
dialex init --framework fastify --default-locale en --locales en,tr -y
```

This creates `dialex.config.ts`, a starter dictionary `src/home.content.ts`, adds `dialexjs` and `@dialexjs/cli` to your `package.json`, and adds a `dx:generate` script (`dx generate`). See [`dialex init`](../cli/init.md).

## Define a dictionary

```ts
// src/home.content.ts
import { defineDictionary } from "dialexjs";

export default defineDictionary("home", {
  en: {
    title: "Welcome to Dialex!",
    greeting: (name: string) => `Hello, ${name}!`,
  },
  tr: {
    title: "Dialex'e Hoş Geldiniz!",
    greeting: (name: string) => `Merhaba, ${name}!`,
  },
});
```

## Compile

```bash
dialex generate
```

Emits `src/dialex.generated.ts` (the dictionary registry) and `src/dialex-env.d.ts` (type augmentation). Then pick your [framework](../frameworks/README.md).


---

# File: guide/glossary.md

# Glossary

The terms Dialex uses, in alphabetical order, with a link to where each is explained.

| Term                     | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Adapter**              | The `dialexjs/<framework>` entry point that resolves a request's locale and gives your code `getDictionary` and `t`. See [Server adapters](../api/server-adapters.md)                                            |
| **Analysis**             | Reading dictionaries, config and source code from their syntax tree to find problems. It never runs your code. Shared by `dialex check`, the editor and the language server                                      |
| **Argument**             | A named value in an ICU message: `{name}`, `{count, plural, ...}`                                                                                                                                                |
| **Config**               | `dialex.config.ts`: `defaultLocale`, `locales`, `include`, `fallbacks`, `lazy`, `translate`... See [Configuration](./configuration.md)                                                                           |
| **Default locale**       | The locale used when a request or a provider decides nothing else, and the one other locales are compared with. `defaultLocale` in the config                                                                    |
| **Dictionary**           | A named object that maps each locale to its content. Defined with `defineDictionary` in a `*.content.ts` file. See [Dictionaries](./dictionaries.md)                                                             |
| **Diagnostic**           | A problem Dialex reports, with a code, a severity and a message. See [Diagnostics reference](./diagnostics.md)                                                                                                   |
| **Fallback chain**       | The ordered list of locales tried for a key: the locale, its explicit fallbacks, its language without region, then the default locale. See [Fallbacks](./fallbacks.md)                                           |
| **Function message**     | A dictionary value that is a function: `` (name: string) => `Hello, ${name}` ``. Typed by TypeScript                                                                                                             |
| **Generated file**       | `dialex.generated.ts` and `dialex-env.d.ts`, written by `dialex generate`. Never edit them. See [`dialex generate`](../cli/generate.md)                                                                          |
| **Hydration**            | A client framework attaching to server-rendered HTML. The first client render must use the server's locale (`initialLocale`) to match                                                                            |
| **ICU message**          | A string in the ICU MessageFormat syntax, with arguments, `plural`, `select`, numbers and dates. See [ICU Messages](./icu.md)                                                                                    |
| **Key**                  | A name inside one locale of a dictionary. May be nested: `nav.about`                                                                                                                                             |
| **Key path**             | A dictionary name and a key joined with dots: `home.nav.about`. What you pass to `t()`. See [Key Paths](./key-paths.md)                                                                                          |
| **Lazy loading**         | Loading dictionaries on demand instead of bundling them all, with `lazy: true` or `"locale"`. See [Lazy Loading](./lazy-loading.md)                                                                              |
| **Leaf**                 | A value in a dictionary that is not an object: a string, a function or another value                                                                                                                             |
| **Locale**               | A language tag such as `en`, `tr` or `pt-BR`                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Lock file**            | `dialex.lock.json`: records which source text each translation was made from, so a later change of the source is noticed. See [Keeping translations in sync](../cli/translate.md#keeping-translations-in-sync)   |
| **Parity**               | Every locale of a dictionary having the same keys (and the same ICU arguments). Checked by `dialex check`                                                                                                        |
| **Persist**              | Remembering the user's locale choice in a cookie or `localStorage`                                                                                                                                               |
| **Plural category**      | One of `zero`, `one`, `two`, `few`, `many`, `other`: the forms a language's plural rules distinguish (CLDR)                                                                                                      |
| **Provider**             | A component or plugin of a UI framework that holds the active locale, such as `DialexProvider`                                                                                                                   |
| **Registry**             | The `DictionaryRegistry` interface that `dialex-env.d.ts` fills with your dictionary names and types. See [Types](../api/types.md)                                                                               |
| **Source locale**        | The locale a translation was made from, usually the default locale. `translate.sourceLocale`                                                                                                                     |
| **Stale translation**    | A translation whose source text changed after it was translated, according to the lock file                                                                                                                      |
| **Static analysis**      | Reading code without running it. Dictionaries and configs written with literals can be read statically; spreads, computed keys and imports cannot. See [Dictionaries](./dictionaries.md#what-the-tools-can-read) |
| **`[TODO]` placeholder** | The prefix `dialex check --fix` puts on a copied string so it is easy to find and translate                                                                                                                      |


---

# File: guide/icu.md

# ICU Messages

Strings in a dictionary can be [ICU MessageFormat](https://unicode-org.github.io/icu/userguide/format_parse/messages/) messages. Pass a values object to `t` and Dialex formats the message for the active locale.

```ts
import { defineDictionary } from "dialexjs";

export default defineDictionary("cart", {
  en: {
    items: "{count, plural, =0 {No items} one {# item} other {# items}}",
    owner: "Hello, {name}!",
  },
  ru: {
    items: "{count, plural, one {# товар} few {# товара} many {# товаров} other {# товара}}",
    owner: "Здравствуйте, {name}!",
  },
});
```

```ts
t("cart.items", { count: 5 }); // en: "5 items"   ru: "5 товаров"
t("cart.owner", { name: "Ada" }); // "Hello, Ada!"
t("cart.owner"); // type error: this message needs { name }
```

ICU messages work next to plain strings and [function values](./dictionaries.md#values); nothing changes for existing dictionaries. Messages are parsed once and cached.

## Syntax

| Syntax        | Example                                                                                      | Notes                                                                                                                     |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Argument      | `{name}`                                                                                     | Any value; converted with `String()`                                                                                      |
| Number        | `{n, number}`, `{n, number, integer}`, `{n, number, percent}`, `{n, number, ::currency/USD}` | `Intl.NumberFormat`                                                                                                       |
| Date, time    | `{d, date, long}`, `{d, time, short}`                                                        | Styles `short`, `medium` (default), `long`, `full`; value is a `Date`, timestamp or date string                           |
| Plural        | `{n, plural, =0 {none} one {# item} other {# items}}`                                        | `=N` exact matches, then the locale's CLDR categories (`zero`, `one`, `two`, `few`, `many`, `other`). `other` is required |
| Plural offset | `{n, plural, offset:1 =0 {nobody} one {you and # other} other {you and # others}}`           | `#` and the categories use `n - offset`; `=N` matches the original `n`                                                    |
| Ordinal       | `{n, selectordinal, one {#st} two {#nd} few {#rd} other {#th}}`                              | Ordinal plural rules                                                                                                      |
| Select        | `{gender, select, female {She} male {He} other {They}}`                                      | Matches the value as a string. `other` is required                                                                        |
| `#`           | inside a plural branch                                                                       | The formatted number. A `select` nested in a plural still refers to the enclosing plural                                  |
| Quoting       | `'{'`, `'}'`, `''`                                                                           | `''` is an apostrophe. A single `'` that does not precede a brace is literal text                                         |

Branches can contain any of the above, so plurals and selects nest.

### Not supported

- Rich-text tags such as `<b>…</b>` are not interpreted; they are plain text.
- Number skeletons other than `::percent` and `::currency/XXX`, and date skeletons, are not supported. Unknown number or date styles fall back to the default style.

## Errors

If a message cannot be formatted, for example because a value is missing, `t` logs a warning and returns the message unchanged, so a bad string never crashes a page. `formatMessage` itself throws `IcuFormatError` (missing or invalid values) or `IcuSyntaxError` (with a position).

```ts
import { formatMessage } from "dialexjs";

formatMessage("en", "{count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}", { count: 3 });
```

## Types

After `dx generate`, the arguments of each message are type-checked: `t("cart.items", { count: 5 })` needs a numeric `count`. `plural`, `selectordinal` and `number` arguments are `number`, `date` and `time` are `Date | number`, `select` is the union of its options (other values are still allowed), and a plain `{name}` accepts a string, number, boolean or `Date`. The types come from the default locale, and [`dialex check`](../cli/check.md) makes sure the other locales use the same arguments. Strings without arguments take no values, and function keys keep their own parameter types.

## Tooling

- [`dialex check`](../cli/check.md) reports invalid ICU, locales that use different arguments than the default locale, and plural options missing for a language (Russian needs `few` and `many`, for example).
- [`dialex translate`](../cli/translate.md) keeps the structure intact: arguments, types, `select` keys and exact `=N` matches must survive, while plural categories may change. Providers that cannot do this (DeepL) never receive ICU messages.
- [`dialex import`](../cli/import.md) rejects values that are invalid ICU or that change the arguments of the same key in another locale.
- [`dialex export`](../cli/export.md) writes ICU messages as plain strings. Ask translators to keep everything inside `{ }` structure and translate only the text in branches.


---

# File: guide/key-paths.md

# Key Paths (`t`)

`t` reads a value by dot path, in addition to `getDictionary(name).key`. It is typed from the generated registry, so paths autocomplete and argument types are checked.

```ts
t("home.title"); // "Welcome"
t("home.nav.about"); // nested objects use more dots
t("home.greeting", "Ada"); // function leaves receive the extra arguments
```

If the leaf is a string and you pass a values object, it is formatted as an [ICU message](./icu.md): `t("cart.items", { count: 3 })`.

Unknown paths log a warning and return the path itself.

## Where it is available

| Environment   | How to get `t`                                             |
| ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| React         | `const t = useT()` from `dialexjs/react`                   |
| Vue / Nuxt    | `const t = useT()` from `dialexjs/vue`                     |
| Server (Next) | `const t = getT(locale)` from `createDialexServer(dialex)` |
| Elysia        | `t` on the request context                                 |
| SvelteKit     | `event.locals.t`                                           |
| Astro         | `Astro.locals.t`                                           |
| Anywhere else | `createT(getDictionary)` from `dialexjs`                   |

## Typing

After `dialex generate`, the registry augments the `dialexjs` module, so `TranslationPath` becomes a union such as `"home.title" | "home.greeting" | "home.nav.about"`. Passing an unknown path or the wrong argument type is a compile error:

```ts
t("home.greeting", 42); // Error: number is not assignable to string
t("home.nope"); // Error: not a valid path
```

Before the registry is generated, `t` accepts any string.


---

# File: guide/lazy-loading.md

# Lazy Loading

By default every dictionary is bundled up front. With `lazy: true`, `dx generate` writes dynamic imports instead of static ones, so your bundler splits each dictionary file into its own chunk and the provider loads it when a component first needs it. This applies to [React / Vite](../frameworks/react.md) and [Vue / Nuxt](../frameworks/vue.md). Next.js already splits code per route, the server adapters read dictionaries directly, and [Angular](../frameworks/angular.md) receives its dictionaries explicitly, so they are unaffected.

```ts
// dialex.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  defaultLocale: "en",
  locales: ["en", "tr"],
  lazy: true,
});
```

::: warning Granularity
With `lazy: true` splitting is **per dictionary file**: each file defines all of its locales together, so loading one dictionary loads every locale of it. Use `lazy: "locale"` (below) to split per locale as well.
:::

## Per locale

With `lazy: "locale"`, `dx generate` also splits each dictionary per locale, so a visitor only downloads the language they read:

```ts
// dialex.config.ts
export default defineConfig({
  locales: ["en", "tr"],
  lazy: "locale",
});
```

The per-locale modules are written to a `dialex.locales/` folder next to `dialex.generated.ts`. Commit them like the generated file; [`dialex check`](../cli/check.md) reports missing or out-of-date ones. Switching language downloads the new locale on demand, and in React the current language stays on screen until the new one has arrived (the update runs in a transition). `preloadDictionaries(dialex, { locale: "tr" }, "pricing")` fetches ahead of time.

A dictionary is split only when each locale is self-contained. If a locale uses something defined elsewhere in the file (an import or a helper), `dx generate` keeps that dictionary whole and says why.

## React

`useDictionary` suspends until the dictionary has loaded, so render it under `<Suspense>`:

```tsx
import { useDictionary, useT, preloadDictionaries } from "dialexjs/react";
import { Suspense } from "react";

import { dialex } from "./dialex.generated";

function Pricing() {
  const dict = useDictionary("pricing"); // suspends on first use
  return <h1>{dict.title}</h1>;
}

function Nav() {
  const t = useT("nav"); // name the dictionaries `t` will read
  return <a>{t("nav.about")}</a>;
}

<Suspense fallback={<Spinner />}>
  <Pricing />
</Suspense>;

// e.g. on hover, to avoid the fallback:
preloadDictionaries(dialex, "pricing");
```

`t("dict.key")` cannot suspend on its own, so `useT` takes the names of the dictionaries it will read. A name that is not loaded yet logs a warning and returns the path.

## Vue

`useDictionary` returns a `ComputedRef` that is empty until the dictionary loads, then updates. During server-side rendering the render waits for it.

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { useDictionary, preloadDictionaries } from "dialexjs/vue";

const dict = useDictionary("pricing");
</script>

<template>
  <h1>{{ dict.title }}</h1>
</template>
```

Use `useT("pricing")` the same way, and `preloadDictionaries(dialex, "pricing")` in a route guard.

## Notes

- A dictionary's name is read from the source text without running it, so lazy mode needs `defineDictionary("name", ...)` or a literal `name: "..."` property. Otherwise `dx generate` fails with a message naming the file.
- Lazy mode is for client bundles: the generated `dictionaries` export is empty, so `createDialexServer` and the server adapters need an eager generated file.
- Load results are cached per dictionary.


---

# File: guide/linting.md

# Linting with ESLint and oxlint

`@dialexjs/eslint-plugin` reports Dialex problems where your other lint errors already are: in the terminal, in CI and in any editor that runs ESLint or oxlint. It is one package for both linters, because oxlint loads ESLint-style plugins.

It needs a `dialex.config.*` above the file being linted and does nothing in projects without one. Like `dialex check`, it reads dictionaries and the config from the syntax tree and never runs project code.

## ESLint

Install it, then add its config to `eslint.config.js`:

```sh
npm install --save-dev @dialexjs/eslint-plugin
```

```js
import dialex from "@dialexjs/eslint-plugin";

export default [dialex.configs.recommended];
```

## oxlint

oxlint has no shareable configs, so list the plugin and the rules yourself in `.oxlintrc.json`:

```json
{
  "jsPlugins": ["@dialexjs/eslint-plugin"],
  "rules": {
    "dialex/no-unknown-dictionary": "error",
    "dialex/no-unknown-path": "error",
    "dialex/no-dynamic-key": "warn",
    "dialex/valid-dictionary": "error"
  }
}
```

oxlint's JS plugins are in alpha, and it does not run plugin rules on `.vue`, `.svelte` or `.astro` files. `dialex check` and the editor extensions still cover those.

## Rules

| Rule                           | Reports                                                                                                       | `recommended` |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| `dialex/no-unknown-dictionary` | `getDictionary("x")`, `useDictionary("x")` or `@DialexDictionary("x")` names a dictionary that does not exist | `error`       |
| `dialex/no-unknown-path`       | `t("a.nope")` where `a` is a known dictionary but has no such key                                             | `error`       |
| `dialex/no-dynamic-key`        | A dictionary name or key that is not a string literal, so Dialex cannot check it                              | `warn`        |
| `dialex/valid-dictionary`      | What `dialex check` finds in a dictionary file                                                                | `error`       |
| `dialex/no-literal-string`     | Text written in JSX instead of coming from a dictionary                                                       | off           |

### no-unknown-dictionary

The same check as the `unknown-dictionary` diagnostic. A dictionary registered in code with `dictionaries: { name: ... }` counts as known, and comments are never checked.

### no-unknown-path

The same check as `unknown-path`. Keys of dictionaries Dialex does not know are ignored, because `t()` may belong to another library.

### no-dynamic-key

`getDictionary(name)` and ``t(`home.${key}`)`` cannot be verified. A bare `t` is only checked in files that import from `dialexjs`, since other libraries use that name too.

### valid-dictionary

Runs on dictionary files, on the text in the editor, and reports the dictionary [codes](./diagnostics.md) such as `missing-key`, `missing-locale`, `invalid-icu` and `todo-placeholder`. Unused keys and dictionaries are left to `dialex check`, which sees the whole project. Skip codes with `ignore`:

```json
{ "dialex/valid-dictionary": ["error", { "ignore": ["todo-placeholder"] }] }
```

### no-literal-string

Flags JSX text that contains letters and the values of `title`, `alt`, `placeholder`, `aria-label` and `label`. It is off in `recommended` because most projects have some text that is fine to keep. Options:

```json
{
  "dialex/no-literal-string": [
    "warn",
    { "attributes": ["title", "alt"], "ignore": ["^OK$"], "ignoreComponents": ["Trans", "code"] }
  ]
}
```

`attributes` replaces the attribute list, `ignore` is a list of regular expressions matched against the trimmed text, and `ignoreComponents` names elements whose content is skipped (by default `Trans`, `code`, `pre`, `script` and `style`).

## Configuration

Rules are configured once, under `lint.rules` in `dialex.config.ts`. `dialex check`, the editor extensions and these ESLint and oxlint rules all read it, so a check is on or off, with the same options, everywhere.

```ts
import { defineConfig } from "dialexjs";

export default defineConfig({
  defaultLocale: "en",
  locales: ["en", "tr"],
  lint: {
    rules: {
      "unused-key": "off",
      "missing-key": "warn",
      "literal-string": ["warn", { ignore: ["^OK$"] }],
    },
  },
});
```

Keys are the [diagnostic codes](./diagnostics.md), plus `dynamic-key` and `literal-string`, which only the linter plugin evaluates. A value is `"off"`, `"warn"`, `"error"` or `[level, options]`. The level changes how `dialex check` and the editors report the issue. In ESLint it is the severity that `dialex.configs.recommended` gives the rule, read from the `dialex.config.*` in the directory ESLint runs in, and `literal-string` is only on in `recommended` when you set it here.

oxlint reads severities from `.oxlintrc.json`, which cannot be computed, so list the rules there at the level you want. `"off"` and options from `dialex.config.ts` still apply, so a check you turn off there stays quiet. `valid-dictionary` is one rule for many codes and the linter shows it at one level; per-code levels apply in `dialex check` and the editors. Options passed to a rule in the linter's own config override those from `dialex.config.ts`.

## Suppressing a report

Use the linter's own comments, such as `// eslint-disable-next-line dialex/no-unknown-dictionary`. The `dialex-ignore` comments from [Diagnostics](./diagnostics.md) are for `dialex check` and the editors, and the plugin does not read them.

## Editors

If your editor already shows these problems from ESLint or oxlint, turn off Dialex's own copy so each is shown once. Hover, completion and quick fixes keep working. In VS Code:

```json
{ "dialex.diagnostics": false }
```

In Zed, set `diagnostics` to `false` under `lsp.dialex.settings` ([Zed and other editors](./zed.md)).

# File: guide/locale-detection.md

# Locale Detection

The server adapters (Express, Fastify, Koa, Hono, Elysia, h3, Hapi, AdonisJS, NestJS, SvelteKit, Astro, tRPC and the Fetch API handler) resolve the request locale from several sources, in this order:

1. A custom extractor (`custom`)
2. The first path segment (`/tr/...`), when `usePath` is true and `locales` is configured (without `locales`, the path is ignored so segments like `/api` are never mistaken for a locale; query strings and fragments are stripped before matching)
3. Query parameter (`locale`, `lang`)
4. Cookie (`locale`, `lang`)
5. The `Accept-Language` header

The first candidate that matches a supported locale wins, otherwise `defaultLocale` is used. `Accept-Language` entries with `q=0` are ignored, and a malformed percent-encoding in a cookie value is used as-is instead of raising an error.

## Options

All adapters accept these (`LocaleResolverOptions`):

| Option          | Type                                   | Default              | Description                                                                             |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `defaultLocale` | `string`                               | `"en"`               | Fallback locale                                                                         |
| `locales`       | `string[]`                             | —                    | Supported locales                                                                       |
| `queryKeys`     | `string \| string[]`                   | `["locale", "lang"]` | Query parameter names                                                                   |
| `cookieKeys`    | `string \| string[]`                   | `["locale", "lang"]` | Cookie names                                                                            |
| `headerKey`     | `string`                               | `"Accept-Language"`  | Header to read                                                                          |
| `usePath`       | `boolean`                              | `true`               | Check the first URL path segment                                                        |
| `custom`        | `(req) => string \| null \| undefined` | —                    | Custom extractor                                                                        |
| `config`        | `GeneratedConfig`                      | —                    | The generated config. Fills `defaultLocale`, `locales` and `fallbacks` that are not set |
| `fallbacks`     | `Record<string, string[]>`             | —                    | Explicit [fallback chains](./fallbacks.md)                                              |

Besides these, every adapter takes `dictionaries` (a map or an array of `defineDictionary` results; without it the dictionaries registered by `defineDictionary` are used) and `setHeader` (default `true`; sends `Content-Language`). Options you pass explicitly win over the generated `config`, and the generated `config` wins over the defaults. Every option, adapter by adapter, is on [Server adapters](../api/server-adapters.md).

## Matching rules

`matchLocale` is case-insensitive and tries, in order: exact match, language prefix of the candidate (`en-US` → `en`), then supported locale with matching prefix (`en` → `en-US`).

## Response header

With `setHeader` (the default) the resolved locale is sent as `Content-Language`. If a CDN or proxy caches pages that depend on `Accept-Language`, also send `Vary: Accept-Language`.

## Helpers

Internally the adapters share `parseAcceptLanguage`, `matchLocale`, `resolveLocaleFromCandidates`, `extractCookieLocale`, and `extractPathLocale`. These live in `src/resolver.ts` and are not part of the package's public `exports`.

# File: guide/migration.md

# Migrating to Dialex

How to move from i18next, react-intl (FormatJS), next-intl or vue-i18n. The ideas map closely; what changes is where messages live (TypeScript files, not JSON) and how you call them (one `t` with the dictionary name first).

## The plan

1. **Install** `dialexjs` and `@dialexjs/cli`, and run `dialex init` ([Getting Started](./getting-started.md)).
2. **Create one dictionary per namespace or feature**, with an empty object per locale:

   ```ts
   // src/home.content.ts
   import { defineDictionary } from "dialexjs";

   export default defineDictionary("home", { en: {}, tr: {} });
   ```

3. **Flatten your JSON** to one file per locale with keys prefixed by the dictionary name, then **import** it:

   ```json
   { "home.title": "Welcome", "home.nav.about": "About" }
   ```

   ```bash
   dialex import en.json --allow-new
   dialex import tr.json --allow-new
   ```

   `--allow-new` adds keys that no locale has yet. [`dialex import`](../cli/import.md) validates ICU messages and lists what it rejected.

4. **Convert the message syntax** (next section) in the dictionaries.
5. **Replace the calls** in your code, one framework at a time.
6. **Run `dialex generate` and `dialex check`.** Missing keys, mismatched arguments and calls to keys that do not exist show up immediately.

## Message syntax

Dialex messages are [ICU MessageFormat](./icu.md). If your messages are already ICU, copy them.

| You have                                               | Write in Dialex                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| i18next `Hello {{name}}`                               | `Hello {name}`                                                                                                            |
| i18next `key_one` / `key_other` with `{{count}}`       | `{count, plural, one {# item} other {# items}}`                                                                           |
| i18next context `key_male` / `key_female`              | `{gender, select, male {...} female {...} other {...}}`                                                                   |
| i18next nesting `$t(other.key)`                        | No equivalent. Repeat the text, or use a function message that calls `t`                                                  |
| i18next formatting `{{val, number}}`                   | `{val, number}`; dates `{when, date, medium}`                                                                             |
| vue-i18n `{name}`                                      | The same                                                                                                                  |
| vue-i18n pipes `no items \| one item \| {count} items` | `{count, plural, =0 {no items} one {one item} other {# items}}`                                                           |
| vue-i18n linked `@:other.key`                          | No equivalent. Repeat the text                                                                                            |
| react-intl and next-intl ICU strings                   | The same, copied as they are                                                                                              |
| Rich text tags `<b>...</b>`                            | **Not supported**: tags are not parsed. Split the message around the markup, or write a function message that returns JSX |

## From i18next

| i18next                                | Dialex                                                                      |
| -------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `locales/<lng>/<ns>.json`              | `src/<ns>.content.ts`: `defineDictionary("<ns>", { en: {...}, tr: {...} })` |
| `useTranslation("home")`, `t("title")` | `useT("home")`, `t("home.title")`: the dictionary name is part of the path  |
| `i18n.changeLanguage("tr")`            | `setLocale("tr")` from `useDialex()`                                        |
| `i18n.language`                        | `locale` from `useDialex()`                                                 |
| `fallbackLng`                          | `defaultLocale` and `fallbacks` in `dialex.config.ts`                       |
| `supportedLngs`                        | `locales`                                                                   |
| Language detector plugin               | The server adapters, or the provider's `initialLocale` and `persist`        |
| Lazy-loaded backends                   | `lazy: true` or `"locale"`; see [Lazy Loading](./lazy-loading.md)           |

```tsx
// before
const { t } = useTranslation("home");
return <p>{t("items", { count })}</p>;

// after
const t = useT("home");
return <p>{t("home.items", { count })}</p>;
```

## From react-intl (FormatJS)

| react-intl                                                            | Dialex                                                                                          |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Message catalog `{ "home.title": "..." }`                             | The same flat keys: `dialex import` takes them as they are (`home` becomes the dictionary)      |
| `<IntlProvider locale messages>`                                      | `<DialexProvider {...dialex}>`                                                                  |
| `intl.formatMessage({ id }, values)`, `<FormattedMessage>`            | `t("home.title", values)`                                                                       |
| `defineMessages`, message extraction                                  | Not needed: keys live in the dictionary, and `dialex check` finds unknown ones                  |
| `intl.formatNumber`, `formatDate`, `formatRelativeTime`, `formatList` | `number`, `date`, `relativeTime`, `list` from `dialexjs`, with the locale as the first argument |
| `intl.locale`                                                         | `locale` from `useDialex()`                                                                     |

```tsx
// before
<FormattedMessage id="home.items" values={{ count }} />;

// after
{
  t("home.items", { count });
}
```

## From next-intl

| next-intl                               | Dialex                                                             |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `messages/<locale>.json`                | `*.content.ts` dictionaries (flatten and `dialex import` the JSON) |
| `useTranslations("home")`, `t("title")` | `useT("home")`, `t("home.title")`                                  |
| `getTranslations` in Server Components  | `getT(locale)` from `createDialexServer(dialex)`                   |
| `createMiddleware(routing)`             | `createDialexMiddleware({ locales, defaultLocale })`               |
| `Link` from `createNavigation`          | `DialexLink`                                                       |
| `t.rich(...)`                           | Not supported. Use a function message that returns JSX             |
| `NextIntlClientProvider`                | `DialexProvider {...dialex}`                                       |

See [Next.js](../frameworks/nextjs.md) for the complete setup.

## From vue-i18n

| vue-i18n                                  | Dialex                                                             |
| ----------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `createI18n({ locale, messages })`        | `createDialex({ ...dialex })` and `app.use(...)`                   |
| `useI18n()`, `t("home.title")`, `$t(...)` | `useT("home")` and `t("home.title")`                               |
| `locale.value = "tr"`                     | `setLocale("tr")` from `useDialex()`                               |
| `fallbackLocale`                          | `defaultLocale` and `fallbacks`                                    |
| Message pipes for plurals                 | ICU `plural`                                                       |
| Nuxt `@nuxtjs/i18n`                       | The `dialexjs/nuxt` module; see [Vue / Nuxt](../frameworks/vue.md) |

## What Dialex does not have

Check these before you start; each has a workaround above.

- Rich text tags in messages (`<b>`, `t.rich`): use function messages that return markup.
- Nested or linked messages (`$t(...)`, `@:key`): repeat the text.
- Namespaces as a separate concept: a dictionary is the namespace.
- Loading translations from a server at runtime: translations ship with the app (see the [FAQ](./faq.md)).
- Pseudo-localization and automatic key extraction from code: keys live in dictionaries, which `dialex check` verifies against your code.

## When you are done

- [ ] `dialex check` exits with `0`
- [ ] `dialex check` runs in CI, so the generated files and the parity stay honest
- [ ] The old i18n packages and their JSON files are removed
- [ ] Editors have the [Dialex extension](./vscode.md), which gives hover and go to definition on `t("...")`

# File: guide/requirements.md

# Requirements

What Dialex needs from your environment, and what it asks you to install yourself.

## Runtime and tooling

| Requirement       | What Dialex needs                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Module format     | The packages are **ES modules only** (`"type": "module"`, `.mjs` files). Import them from ESM, a bundler, or `import()` in CommonJS                                                            |
| Node.js           | No `engines` field is declared. The test suite and the CI run on Node.js 22; the repository's own tooling needs 22.18 or later. Use a current LTS release                                      |
| Other runtimes    | The runtime core and the Fetch API handler use only standard APIs (`Intl`, `Request`, `Headers`, `Map`), so they run where those exist: Bun, Deno, Cloudflare Workers and browsers             |
| TypeScript        | A current 5.x or later. The types use template literal and conditional types. The repository type-checks with TypeScript 7                                                                     |
| Module resolution | `compilerOptions.moduleResolution` must be `"bundler"`, `"node16"` or `"nodenext"`. The subpath imports (`dialexjs/react`) are `exports` entries, which the old `"node"` setting does not read |
| Package manager   | npm, Yarn, pnpm and Bun all work.                                                                                                                                                              |

## Packages

| Package                     | What it is                                        | Dependencies                                    |
| --------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| `dialexjs`                  | The runtime and every framework adapter           | None. Frameworks are optional peer dependencies |
| `@dialexjs/cli`             | `dialex` / `dx`. Install as a dev dependency      | Installs its own tooling; needs `dialexjs`      |
| `@dialexjs/eslint-plugin`   | ESLint and oxlint rules for dictionaries and keys | `@dialexjs/cli`                                 |
| `@dialexjs/language-server` | The LSP server for Zed and other editors          | `@dialexjs/cli`                                 |
| `@dialexjs/mcp`             | The MCP server for AI assistants                  | `@dialexjs/cli`                                 |

## Framework versions

Frameworks are **optional peer dependencies** of `dialexjs`: install only the ones you use. These are the versions the adapters declare:

| Adapter                                                  | Peer dependency                  | Range                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | --------------------- |
| `dialexjs/react`, `react-native`, `next/*` (with `next`) | `react`                          | `>=19.0.0`            |
| `dialexjs/next/middleware`, `next/link`                  | `next`                           | `>=13.0.0`            |
| `dialexjs/preact`                                        | `preact`                         | `>=10.0.0`            |
| `dialexjs/solid`                                         | `solid-js`                       | `^1.8.0`              |
| `dialexjs/vue`                                           | `vue`                            | `^3.4.0`              |
| `dialexjs/nuxt`                                          | `@nuxt/kit`                      | `>=3.0.0`             |
| `dialexjs/svelte`                                        | `svelte`                         | `^4.0.0 \|\| ^5.0.0`  |
| `dialexjs/qwik`                                          | `@builder.io/qwik`               | `>=1.5.0 <2`          |
| `dialexjs/lit`                                           | `lit`                            | `^3.0.0`              |
| `dialexjs/angular`                                       | `@angular/core`, `rxjs`          | `>=17.0.0`, `>=7.0.0` |
| `dialexjs/express`                                       | `express`                        | `>=4.0.0`             |
| `dialexjs/fastify`                                       | `fastify`                        | `>=4.0.0`             |
| `dialexjs/koa`                                           | `koa`                            | `>=2.0.0`             |
| `dialexjs/hono`                                          | `hono`                           | `>=3.0.0`             |
| `dialexjs/elysia`                                        | `elysia`                         | `>=1.0.0`             |
| `dialexjs/nestjs`                                        | `@nestjs/common`, `@nestjs/core` | `>=10.0.0`            |
| `dialexjs/hapi`                                          | `@hapi/hapi`                     | `>=21.0.0`            |
| `dialexjs/adonis`                                        | `@adonisjs/http-server`          | `>=7.0.0`             |
| `dialexjs/h3`                                            | `h3`                             | `>=1.8.0 <2`          |
| `dialexjs/astro`                                         | `astro`                          | `>=4.0.0`             |

`dialexjs/sveltekit`, `dialexjs/trpc`, `dialexjs/web`, `dialexjs/routing`, `dialexjs/icu`, `dialexjs/server` and `dialexjs/testing` need no framework package: they use structural types or standard `Request`s. React Native uses `react`; Expo's `expo-localization` and AsyncStorage are what you pass in, not peer dependencies.

## Editors

| Editor            | What you need                                                                                                           |
| ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| VS Code           | The Dialex extension (a `.vsix` attached to each GitHub release). See [VS Code](./vscode.md)                            |
| Zed               | The Dialex extension; it starts `@dialexjs/language-server`, which needs Node.js. See [Zed and other editors](./zed.md) |
| Anything with LSP | `@dialexjs/language-server`, started with `--stdio`                                                                     |

## Check your setup

```bash
node --version            # a current LTS
npx dialex --version      # the CLI, once installed
npx dialex check          # parity, ICU, references and a stale generated file
```

# File: guide/routing.md

# Routing Helpers

Framework-agnostic helpers for locale-prefixed URLs, from `dialexjs/routing`.

```ts
import {
  localizePath,
  stripLocale,
  alternateLinks,
  alternateLanguages,
  sitemapEntries,
} from "dialexjs/routing";

const options = { locales: ["en", "tr"], defaultLocale: "en" };

localizePath("/about", "tr", options); // "/tr/about"
localizePath("/en/about", "tr", options); // "/tr/about" (an existing prefix is replaced)
stripLocale("/tr/about", ["en", "tr"]); // { path: "/about", locale: "tr" }
```

## `localizePath(path, locale, options)`

Prefixes a path with a locale. Query strings and fragments are kept. External URLs (`https://...`, `//cdn...`), `mailto:` links and bare `#fragments` are returned unchanged.

With `prefixDefault: false` the default locale gets no prefix:

```ts
const asNeeded = { ...options, prefixDefault: false };
localizePath("/about", "en", asNeeded); // "/about"
localizePath("/about", "tr", asNeeded); // "/tr/about"
```

## `stripLocale(path, locales)`

Removes a leading locale segment and tells you which one it was. Only exact, case-insensitive matches count, so `/english/about` is left alone.

## `localeFromPath(path, options)` and `isLocale(value, locales)`

`localeFromPath` returns the locale a path is under, or `defaultLocale` when it has no prefix. `isLocale` checks a string (for example a route param) against your supported locales.

```ts
localeFromPath("/tr/about", options); // "tr"
localeFromPath("/about", options); // "en"
isLocale("tr", options.locales); // true
```

## With your router

`localizePath` needs two things: the locale the app is showing and your router's own navigation function. Every framework page has the full recipe; this is where each one gets them:

| Framework                   | Current locale               | Navigate                                      |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| React Router                | `useDialex().locale`         | `useNavigate()`                               |
| TanStack Router             | `useDialex().locale`         | `useNavigate()`, `{-$locale}` route parameter |
| Next.js                     | `useDialex().locale`         | `useRouter().push()`, `DialexLink`            |
| Vue Router, Nuxt            | `useDialex().locale.value`   | `router.push()`, `navigateTo()`               |
| SvelteKit                   | `$locale` from `useDialex()` | `goto()`, `redirect()`                        |
| Solid Router                | `useDialex().locale()`       | `useNavigate()`                               |
| Preact (preact-iso)         | `useDialex().locale`         | `useLocation().route()`                       |
| Qwik City                   | `useDialex().locale`         | `useNavigate()`                               |
| Angular                     | `injectDialex().locale()`    | `Router.navigateByUrl()`                      |
| Astro                       | `Astro.locals.locale`        | `Astro.redirect()`                            |
| Express, Fastify, Koa, Hono | `req.locale`, `c.var.locale` | `res.redirect()`, `c.redirect()`              |

## hreflang and sitemaps

```ts
const seo = { ...options, baseUrl: "https://example.com" };

alternateLinks("/about", seo);
// [{ locale: "en", href: "https://example.com/en/about" },
//  { locale: "tr", href: "https://example.com/tr/about" },
//  { locale: "x-default", href: "https://example.com/en/about" }]

alternateLanguages("/about", seo); // { en: "...", tr: "...", "x-default": "..." }
sitemapEntries(["/", "/about"], { ...seo, lastModified: "2024-01-01" });
```

`alternateLanguages` matches the shape of Next.js `metadata.alternates.languages`; `sitemapEntries` returns one entry per path and locale, each with `alternates.languages`, matching `MetadataRoute.Sitemap`. Pass `xDefault: false` to leave out `x-default`.

For Next.js there are also [`createDialexMiddleware` and `DialexLink`](../frameworks/nextjs.md).
